title: Good app,  but wish it were better
body:
I am a perimenopausal working mom with ADHD, so I NEED something like this to help me be productive throughout the day and remember things and be my “second brain.”

Overall I really like the app (so much that I got the lifetime subscription), but there are two minor complaints I have when using it. When I add things to my day in the morning, afternoon, or evening blocks, I wish it was easier to drag to reorder the things I need to get done in order of priority or somewhat chronological order without assigning set times to them. I’m not sure if it’s just my app being glitchy, but every time I move one task and then try to move another, it resets everything or puts things in a weird order that I did not want. The other one is the “AI assistant” where you can just brain dump and have it put tasks on your to-do list. It’s fine if you already know your task breakdown, but part of ADHD is not knowing or feeling overwhelmed by big tasks and needing them broken down to smaller components and I wish the AI assistant could help with that instead of making tasks for exactly what I say. For example, if I say “do laundry,” it just makes a task for that, but I wish it would break it out into components like “start a load of laundry,” “move it to the dryer to dry,” “take out and fold laundry,” and “put away folded laundry”. That might be a dumb example, but it illustrates what I’d like to see

title: Still needs tons of improvement on desktop
body:
I really love this app on mobile, but on desktop it’s much harder to do what I do on my phone.

I can’t delete lists on the desktop app, and the emojis glitch in the calendar day view, so it’s hard to see which part of the day you’re in.

I use this app a lot in both my personal and professional life because it makes it easy to see how the day is going and to move activities around. For work, though, it’s not ideal, because the Mac app is much weaker than the iPhone one. Because of that, I have to use the browser, and I can’t keep my work activities up to date easily. My job requires me to have hundreds of tabs open, so I lose track of the app’s tab and of what I need to do. Some days I end up going back to a notepad to remember my tasks, which defeats the main purpose of the app: helping people with ADHD.

Technically, on Mac it’s just one more app for listing tasks, not one that actually helps with ADHD.

title: What happened to the confetti???
body:
Update: one of the things I liked most about this app was the little celebratory confetti effect when I marked a task completed. It was an acknowledgment of effort and helped me stay motivated to keep working towards completing my tasks. Now it’s gone and Tiimo has gone from being genuinely useful to me, and being recommended to others by me, to something utilitarian that can easily be replaced with Apple’s built in reminders App. I’m very disappointed.

I’ve found this app to be helpful in keeping me focused on the things I want to accomplish. I know that it has more capability than I utilize, but I simply don’t need all of it. I do have one complaint and that’s with the frequent push for users to upgrade to premium. I’ve gotten pop ups every time I open the app this week encouraging me to take advantage of a premium subscription discount. It’s very frustrating to have my concentration disrupted by a sales pitch before I’m allowed to add a task. Now, with this most recent update, the option to choose an emoji symbol relevant to my task has been moved behind the premium pay wall. 

I understand that the developers are in business to turn a profit, but the tactic of gradually eliminating functionality feels disingenuous. If it continues, free account users will either feel forced to pay, or give up on the app altogether. I sincerely hope it won’t come to that for me.

The problem is I have a to do list 9 pages long and I don’t know where to begin, what are the priorities- what can be back-burnered.  So I do nothing or I do what’s easy or I hyper-focus on something that could wait while something else is on fire.  I have dozens of apps on my phone that can remind me to do stuff, but building habits takes more than that.  If you need another to-do list, go for it but don’t think this is some kind of game-changing magic bullet because it’s not.

title: Lots of wasted potential
body: I use AI to do my job, so the idea of this app as a light personal assistant seemed like a very useful application of the tech. In practice, this chat bot is really dumb and cannot actually parse a slightly nuanced todo or deal with a big brain dump. You also can only accept or reject its actions, you can’t correct them to tell the LLM what was wrong when the only issue is the time or a misheard word. For example, I said I needed to pick something up on the way home from an appointment, so it scheduled that reminder for 90min after the appointment ended instead of at the end time, but that was so many taps to correct it wasn’t really worth using the AI to begin with. It is not remotely capable of transforming a nebulous description of chores into actionable, scheduled steps, despite basically putting that ability on the tin. It’s really just a purpose built Siri focused only on reminders, and it can do a whole lot less than Siri. Add to that the UI is just plain confusing and unintuitive, things are divided into tabs in the most useless way, and none of the top level tabs feel as useful as they should be. This app feels like work to use when it’s supposed to make things easier.

At least for adhd, it is a fantastic app.

title: I NEVER pay for apps but this was worth it!💜
body:
I NEVER write reviews. Like, EVER. But this app has helped me so much that I had to share it.
I have ADD and other executive functioning challenges, and scheduling has ALWAYS been something I struggled with. I’ve tried all kinds of scheduling apps, but I could never actually schedule in a way that works for me. It always felt like more work just trying to organize my life.
Then I found Tiimo. 🥹
The feature that completely changed the game for me is that I can voice-text my tasks, and Tiimo schedules them for me. I don’t have to sit there and manually enter everything, figure out where it should go, and spend forever organizing my day. I can basically just tell it what I need to do, and it helps me put it into a schedule.
At first, I thought this feature was free, but I eventually found out that I had to pay for it. 😕 As a college student who doesn’t have a lot of extra money—and someone who NEVER, EVER pays for apps—I was honestly pretty disappointed.
But I paid for it anyway.
And It was worth it.
The way this app works has genuinely made scheduling and keeping up with my responsibilities so much easier. I only wish the voice-to-schedule feature was free because I know there are SO many people who struggle with the exact same things I do who could benefit from it.
The basic functions of Tiimo are free, but the voice-to-text scheduling feature—which is the feature that helped me the most—requires a paid plan.
So if you struggle with scheduling, organization, executive functioning, or you’re neurodivergent, I 10/10 recommend giving Tiimo a try. ❤️
And Tiimo, THANK YOU for making something that actually works for people like me. 🙌
Now please make the voice scheduling feature free so more people can use it because I can’t.😭❤️

title: Updated review
body:
I’ve been using Tiimo for over a year now, and I have to say the updates since my last review have been really great. A lot of the things I mentioned before actually feel like they were taken into consideration.

What I love most is that the app keeps its simplicity, but still allows for creativity. I can customize my layout to fit my style without feeling overwhelmed by too many options. The built-in color schemes are vibrant without being “too much,” which makes it fun and motivating to use.

I especially appreciate how the day is divided into morning, day, and evening sections, which keeps things from feeling cluttered. The drop-down lists are another favorite—being able to expand or shorten them makes my schedule feel manageable.

One of the biggest highlights for me has been the new AI integration. I actually suggested this in my original review, so seeing it added was amazing! It’s still new and could be expanded, but it’s already a great feature that makes planning easier.

Since these updates, I’ve been using Tiimo more consistently, and I can honestly say it helps me stay on track throughout the day.

A few things I’d love to see in the future:
	•	More adaptations to the AI features.
	•	A true home screen view—being able to see tasks and check them off directly from my home screen without fully opening the app would be so helpful.
	•	A way to schedule travel time between activities, so that “empty space” actually reflects the time I spend driving or transitioning, not just free time.

Overall, Tiimo is still my favorite ADHD/autism-friendly planner. It’s colorful, simple, and motivating, and I can see it only getting better from here.

title: ADHD friendly claim is laughable
body:
Everything is focused on the AI agent instead of actually improving the app. Asking me to provide personal details of my daily life to a robot that will hold onto that info, learn from it, and distribute as needed must mean I’m no longer their customer. 

Routines are no longer a thing, you have to enter each task over and over again.

Calendar sync is PER DEVICE, not per account. I have everything synced on my phone, but the web and ipad apps don’t have those tasks listed without linking calendars to literally every place I could log in. I know it’s possible, Structured is able to do this. 
 
Editing the name of a task updates the icon/color, even when manually set. If you copy a task (because you have it set up how you like) and then edit ANY PART of the name, the icon changes. 

Also, speaking of icons, for calendar tasks, those come in per calendar and are uneditable. I totally get not being able to edit times, but how helpful is the icon/color if all of my work calendar items are pink🍖?

The ipad app isn’t responsive to different window sizes. I should be able to make the window phone sized to multitask while creating my todo list, but making it smaller makes all the text smaller. 

The watch app is absolutely useless imo. Yes, i can check things off, but most of the time I hit the wrong task. Why not create a complication that shows the current task and time (a la the iphone widgets). That nice picture of the watch on the website? Yeah, that’s not actually in the app. The best you’re gonna get is the live activity banner.

Tl;dr: most of their selling points either aren’t there, don’t work as well as they should (especially when you market to people with executive dysfunction!!), or are pretty much eliminated by all the AI functionality in the app.

title: Ok when it works
body:
I bought the lifetime pro after using it for about a week and I won’t be using it. The basic functions are pretty good. It’s easy to schedule or reschedule a task and the widgets are solid.

Where it falls apart is reliability which is a pretty big deal if you had ADHD. I’m skeptical that it always alerts me as intended, but I can’t say for sure. 

The one I can pinpoint is that the calendar integration is buggy on the best days. Several times I’ve had to delete and reinstall the app to get my calendar events to populate in Tiimo. Or I have to wait 15+ minutes for it to pick up an event. The wait wouldn’t be such a big deal if it just worked consistently, but when I’m waiting to see if it’s working at all, that’s a huge pain.

There is also no way to search your tasks except for using the AI assistant which doesn’t really work. I’ve searched for past tasks by exact name to try to reschedule them and the AI assistant says they don’t exist. Then when I scroll for a few weeks, the task is there with the name I searched for.

It’s probably better for people who like to use the AI assistant to manage more of the scheduling for them, but if you just want a robust ADHD scheduler, I don’t think I’d recommend this one.

title: Great app, but family profiles need better options for integration
body:
Tiimo has been genuinely helpful for my own planning, and I appreciate how clean, focused, and easy it is to use. I also like that I can create multiple profiles for different family members. However, one feature that’s missing for me is a way for those profiles to be connected without being merged.

Right now, each profile is completely separate, so if I want to know what’s on my son’s schedule, I have to switch profiles. I’d love an option to layer other profiles’ events onto my own calendar while keeping them visually distinct.

Some ideas that would make this incredibly useful:

* Show other people’s events in a muted or grayed-out style (or with thinner event blocks) so they’re visible for awareness but don’t compete with my own schedule.
* Let users toggle which family members’ schedules appear.
* Allow a custom color for each person’s events so they’re easy to recognize at a glance.
* Keep ownership separate- the events would only be visible in my timeline, not something I can complete or manage. This would simply help me stay aware of my family’s day.

I’d also love a simple daily meal planning section. It doesn’t need recipes or nutrition tracking- just a small text field for breakfast, lunch, and dinner that’s tied to each day, and ideally could be shared across connected family profiles.

Tiimo is already a great app, and these kinds of family-awareness features would make it much more useful for households. I’d love to see this direction in the future.

title: A-Z Game Changer
body:
There are three features tied for first place. 
- The first is a tiny detail on daily screen that tells me how much time I have between tasks. It has been the most liberating thing I did not understand  
I needed. Like most ADD sufferers if I have an activity planned I can do nothing except check the time until that event begins. This tiny feature means everything to me. It instantly relieves my anxiety because I no longer am constantly calibrating how much time I have before I need to get ready to go. Seriously, this is a ‘quality of daily life’ improvement.
 - Secondly, the AI piece.
You literally CAN empty your brain by speaking (no typing) of alllll the things you would love to get done so you can stop replaying them in your head for fear of forgetting the more random/potentially satisfying ones … And a list that you can check off is created FOR you. Dampens dread & overwhelm by 95%.
That’s a dream come true.

title: Predatory “Get Pro” button
body:
Attempting to use the unpaid version of the app subjects the user to an animated “Get Pro” button on a 3 second animation loop. It sits at the top of the Todo and Reminder views and clicking on it once does not silence the animation. This is a predatory practice used in free to play mobile games and has no place in an app allegedly designed with neurodivergent users as a first class customer.

The presence of an attention hostile gimmick is immediately disqualifying, and only goes unnoticed by the broader community because the onboarding workflow conceals it. (require account to capture name and email address -> brief user relief to select desired workflows -> full screen Pro subscription upsell with trial -> “Buy Now” animation only gets observed if user didn’t avoided the trial)

Normally I would not ascribe this workflow to deliberate manipulation, but the fact that the Get Pro button never surfaced in my research indicates that it is either a new addition or has successfully prevented the majority of reviewers from observing it.

Hard pass from me. A company doesn’t get to claim best interests for the neurodivergent and then use this in their UI design. It’s twice damning because it means they know exactly what they are doing.

title: Best UNHELPFUL ADHD app!
body:

When asked why, Tiimo replied it could speak in English if that’s what we wanted. 🤦‍♀️🤦‍♂️When asked what it said in German it ignores the question until we repeated its, and it’s was asking for approval. The schedule it provided for today was labeled “Yesterday”. When asked why, Tiimo replied we’re working on today’s schedule don’t worry about yesterday. Wow! 🤯 AuDHDer’s have energy usage cycles and the Tiimo app burned every bit of morning energy in less than an hour! Finally, which should have been mentioned 1st is that an app (Tiimo) meant to help people who struggle with planning and follow through doesn’t have a built in reminder to let you know when you free 7-day trial will expire, and Tiimo actually tells you, you’ll have to check on that yourself!🤦‍♀️🤦‍♂️🤣😑👎! So needless to say we’ve cancelled already. Just for the sake of it since week
we’re still in the 1st hour of our free trial, we attempted to set up a reminder, six days from now to check on the cancellation of Tiimo. We received 6 reminders for each day, over the next 6 days, to check on cancellation,  excluding “Tiimo” as was requested as a part of the reminder! Yes, DISAPPOINTED and DISSATISFIED with Tiimo, recommending ADHDer’s AVOID Tiimo unless you need some MORE ANXIETY in your schedule. Maybe we should work on producing an app🤔

title: Absolute Game Changer
body:
I don’t write reviews for things. Except clothes sites that give me points. I’ve never written a review for an app. This one, though, is literally life changing for me and my neurodivergent brain!

I’ve tried everything. Paper planners. Checklists. ToDoist. Asana. Notion. All of the top rated project management apps and tools that everyone swears by, and I thought I was broken. I was losing my mind trying to stay on top of things in my very chaotic job and in my everyday life. 

This app has changed everything. It’s set up in a way that is coherent and structured enough for the part of my brain that craves that, and flexible enough to cater to the part of my brain that violently pushes back on said structure. Having a calendar to keep track of deadlines and recurring tasks (and that only shows three days at a time!), along with a running to-do list in sight is exactly what I didn’t know I needed. I keep the web page pinned in my browser on my work computer and the widget on my phone keeps my list in sight and front of mind. Plus a built-in pomodoro timer? I love it!

Thank you all so much for developing this! If y’all come up with a budgeting app for us ND folks, you’d have my money for that one, too.

title: NOT for ADHD brain, wasted so much time trying to set up
body: Not good for this ADHD brain! I wanted to use this to schedule tasks and keep from getting sidetracked, but instead I’m practically in tears after wasting over an hour trying to set up my schedule. I used the AI “Co-Planner” and spoke out what I need to get done today, and it did add everything to my task list but didn’t suggest specific time slots as I had expected. I tried using the Co-Planner to edit and add time slots to all of the tasks (plan my day for me, as I thought this app was supposed to do), but it says I don’t have anything planned! I asked it to change the time of a scheduled task and it asks for the title of the task, then says it can’t find the task! The only way to change anything is to manually go into each task and update the time/duration, which I already have the option to do on my calendar app FOR FREE! The AI feature is also super slow on both PC and iPhone, and it stopped responding completely when I tried using it on my phone. Visually, I can see it being useful IF and ONLY IF it were easier to set up a schedule in the first place. I’m really disappointed in all of the ADHD/AuDHD influencers out there who have recommended this app and I feel like the good reviews have to be phony. I can’t see how anyone with a neurodivergent brain could honestly say this app helped them, unless they have someone else doing the setup and scheduling. Now I’ve wasted even more time writing this review so others with a brain like mine don’t suffer the same fate!

title: Update Suggestion
body:
I love this app. It has been one of the most helpful tools for keeping my day organized and keeping me on track when my mind would otherwise drift, especially on my phone where there are so many distractions.

One of the most useful features for me is the live countdown timer at the top of the iPhone screen. Having that timer constantly visible is honestly one of the biggest reasons the app helps me stay focused and follow through on what I planned for the day.

My main suggestions for a future update are about usability and staying on track throughout the day. First, when other Live Activities are also active, the smaller Tiimo Live Activity is mostly just an icon with a circular countdown bar around it. I think it would be much more helpful if the small Live Activity showed the actual time remaining in the center, with or without the circular bar around it. For me, seeing the actual timer is much more useful than just seeing a visual progress ring. The number gives a clearer sense of how much time is left and makes it easier to stay directed and intentional, especially near the end of a task. I’ve seen other apps implement this effectively, and it makes a big difference in staying aware of time and maintaining focus.

Second, I would really appreciate the ability to manually reorder tasks for the day without having to assign each one a specific time. Sometimes what is most helpful is not scheduling every task by the clock, but simply being able to set them in a clear sequence and work through them one by one. That takes away the mental burden of deciding what to do next and makes it much easier to stay on track.

Overall, I really love the app and appreciate how much it helps. These additions would make an already great app even better.

title: Great concept, but the AI assistant is not yet reliable
body:
I started using Tiimo because the AI assistant sounded like exactly what I needed. When it works, it’s genuinely helpful — it created manageable task steps and suggested ways to declutter my schedule. After a few good experiences, I was honestly ready to leave a glowing review.

Then today happened.

I asked the assistant to break a complex task into 10–15 minute steps spaced throughout my day so I could work in short bursts with breaks — a task the AI assistant is specifically designed and marketed to do.

Instead, the assistant repeatedly failed to recognize the task that already existed in my schedule, confused it with unrelated tasks, and kept asking for information I had already provided.

Even when it created subtasks, they were still much larger than the time blocks I requested. When I asked for smaller steps, the process repeatedly reset rather than refining the plan. At one point it even asked for an internal “activity ID,” which isn’t something a normal user would have.

What should have taken seconds turned into nearly an hour of trying to guide the AI through something it is specifically supposed to help with.

This issue appears reproducible when asking the assistant to break down an existing scheduled task into short time-blocked steps.

The core app itself seems thoughtfully designed, and the concept behind the AI assistant is excellent. But since the assistant is the main reason I tried the app, its unreliability is currently a deal-breaker.

If the AI becomes more consistent, Tiimo could easily be one of the best productivity apps out there.

title: Unfortunately not worth the freemium price
body:
I was originally very excited to discover this app — the accolades and hype made it appear to be the productivity and task tracking tool I had been searching for. At first, it does seem great — the core workflow of brain dumping tasks then scheduling feels very natural and smooth — but after just a few days the bugs and usability red flags begin to show. Below are some examples:

The freemium model is unnecessarily restrictive. With the free version you can create a task, but you need to pay $50+ a year if you want to edit that task.

The AI mode is borderline useless. You ask for help managing tasks and it will spit out a list of all of your tasks. I asked it to create a task called “call dentist office to schedule appointment” and had to go back and forth with the chat it because it ignored the ask and tried to actually create the appointment itself. It also isn’t clear from the chat output whether it actually adds something to your schedule or to your todo as you are always promoted to add a task after AI output..very confusing.

The focus mode is extremely buggy. There is no way to cancel a focus mode. If you have a scheduled task it automatically starts a focus state at that time and you can’t change that preference, which means anything you sync from your calendar or reminders will likely auto start and you will spend your time juggling pausing/unpausing or completing tasks and unchecking to get things to the correct state. You can drag the circle all the way around to complete a focus ring but you can’t drag it part of the way around to speed it up?

Tasks have focus rings but not sub tasks so managing time when there are many sub tasks is a fools errand. 

The best part of the app is what is offered for free. If basic free features weren’t gated by the freemium model, I could see the value in this app because aesthetically it’s probably the best one out there. If you strip away most of what is advertised as “pro” features (AI, lock screen live updates, widgets), I’d be happy with a todo + schedule and reminder notifications and would pay for a lesser subscription cost or lifetime fee.

title: Great interface, needs work
body:
The app is beautiful - good colors, organization, and satisfying UI. However the actual features need much improvement. I bought an annual sub of this app years ago, but it just wasn’t there yet. I came back for it today, just because I do miss the app and wanted to see how much has changed.

1) DRAG & DROP feature on timeline is janky. It is not intuitive. If I have a task scheduled for 4pm, and want to move a different task to right after it, nope. Whatever invisible timeline the spacing is set on is where the task will go. I could move the task after the 4pm one, but it will move to 2am or 3am. I need to keep pulling the task lower and lower, until the small times on left show the correct time, and it could be past 11pm tasks. It is confusing and does not make sense, and sometimes I forget what exact time I want it scheduled at, i just know i wanted it after my other scheduled task! 

2) Would also like a feature to drag duration of tasks, instead of needing to click into it and edit. Too time consuming.

3) What is the point of adding minutes focus time if it doesn’t shift the events after it? Let’s say i have a task with a 30 minute duration. I go over by 7 minutes. Now the rest of my schedule is messed up, obviously i cannot start on my next task if im still focusing on the current one, and i’ll get multiple notifications during my current one, alerting me of upcoming tasks or to start them, when I am 7 minutes behind!! it is overwhelming and ruins the purpose of the focus. They really need to create an automatic shift feature. 

4)  AI chat is useless right now, simply not there yet. I hate how it is at the bottom right, where the most useful button should be, and the new task feature is all the way on the top. Need to switch these two. 

I want this app to work well SOOO badly and have gone back and forth waiting for it to get where it needs to be, but I think this may be the last time I download if these features cannot be updated.

title: Paid AI Features are a massive headache
body:
Don’t get me wrong the concept of the app is great. Without paying for AI Features it’s just another notes app with a todo list format with AI. I thankfully went into this free trial I got knowing from some fairly recent experience how awful AI can’t be at managing a list depending on what certain actions you may request. But then there was glitchiness at times as well as just a pure inability to do simpler tasks like be sure to schedule in a very open morning the task not overlapping something else. I spent a lot more time in the app planning and fighting with the AI to do what I asked then I ever should have.

I’d really like to see something like this succeed but it’s my opinion that making us have to pay for such experimental features is awful, although at the same time I understand the need for a subscription service, but I don’t know what to suggest instead. Because it seems at least ChatGPT has issues with list maybe another AI if that’s what your using or just work towards solutions and call your AI as ai highly suggest “experimental” because that is what it is. Bad at lists or not I made similar requests to ChatGPT directly and it did it far better job then the app. 

I think I’ll just use my $20 a month for ChatGPT that I already pay for anyway to do this apps job. I’ll have half the issues. A headache still, but oh well. 

I really hope one day this AI can feel much more capable and so can use this or another app like it because when things went well it was really nice to use

title: Maybe I missed something but…
body:
I am genuinely shocked by the effusive praise that the app has received. I downloaded it expecting something that would, at a minimum, feel useful. Yet, the app simply created additional friction in what could have been a great consolidator. The challenge is high, replace an ecosystem of time management and organizational apps. So, this should at the very least be as good as those other experiences. Additionally, it brands itself as particularly useful for people with ADHD — which I had been clinically diagnosed with, so it should be perfect, right? Wrong. Consider these three examples as how I knew the app wasn’t for me and that ultimately made it feel more gimmicky than actually useful:
1. I have a daily commute during which I regularly lose service. This also happens to be a great time to mess around with my schedule. For me, understanding context dependent patterns of behavior has been a huge win for helping me work with my sometimes floaty attention. The problem is, even basic things — like moving a past event/item from a previous day to the present day — cannot be done without an active internet connection.
2. I work Monday-Friday and thought it would be useful to have a high level to do list. Things like making the bed, reading a few times a week, exercise, and time to level up outside of work. Editing this schedule is incredibly tedious and requires repeated back and forth with the AI agent or manual editing of the schedule. When I took a week off of work to travel, or for Christmas a few weeks later, I should have been able to tell the agent to remove my tasks for those days. In the case of the former it repeatedly failed leaving me to do it manually. In the case of the latter it removed events on the wrong two days after confirming the correct days. I needed to manually shift over the events. Is there a universe where this just works? Sure. But my experience was that I wasted more time checking its work.
3. Remember that Christmas example from before? Well it turns out that somewhere in the process of rescheduling the time off to the correct days I managed to remove all subsequent occurrences of all my events/tasks. That would make it the second time I had to re-enter my entire schedule. Why manually? Because the agent is slow, imprecise, and inconsistent. It’s just faster to do it myself and to make tweaks with the agent, accept it’s not actually intelligent enough to understand and therefore not intelligent enough to manage my schedule/tasks. Occasionally it was brilliant, but more often than not it was a hassle to use. 

There are also subtle things like the way my tasks shift in importance and prominence throughout a day or week that make it feel less useful, especially because there’s a missed opportunity for 1) giving feedback about when you actually manage to finish things, 2) what you do and don’t finish, 3) meaningful capture and integration of your scheduling goals into your interactions with the agent, or 4) just finding ways to leverage research and other user experiences to give feedback or suggestions.

All in all, not a great user experience for me. It seems to be doing well with many others, but personally I found it was less efficient that just using my phone’s built in calendar and reminder system, which also works using “AI” voice controls. 

I would recommend more traditional methods of managing time for people with ADHD and to try this as an experiment, coming in with low expectations and allowing yourself to be surprised. 

It is not going to solve the more difficult problems of attention, motivation, energy, or time management. It may help but it may not. It seems, at best, a useful tool, given that you can find the right place for it in your toolkit. If you’re anything like me, it will eventually become a source of anxiety and annoyance as you learn to rely on it less and less. After a month or so of trying it out, it’s a no for me.

title: Solid base, but still needs a lot of UX improvements
body:
This app would be great, and I can see it becoming great in the long run if they act quickly to improve the UI/UX. 

First, it's laggy sometimes, specially when editing or creating tasks.

Second, there's no organized way to see all of the "routines" you created, they just show up on your daily view IF they're scheduled. I would think an app that creates routines would easily have a way to let me view and edit them all.

Third, given the way it's designed, it's a hassle to "schedule" your routines to a set time if they don't have a set beginning and ending time that remains the same everyday. I would think you would be able to just easily drag and drop an unscheduled/anytime routine into your calendar, but no, that is not possible, you have to edit it and go through a number of steps to accomplish that, and it's a dealbreaker for me.

Last but not least, even though you have created and set a routine for "morning", "afternoon" or "evening" to repeat daily or at a certain frequency, it doesn't make a difference, because it's always going to be bundled up with the rest of the "anytime" tasks.

Overall, the idea is great, and I really do believe they are targeting a market that is still searching for a better product, because there are many of apps like this out there, and none of them are a perfect fit. However, I'm not sure they are taking advantage of that gap properly. 

This apps feels like an early product of a startup, definitely not the first, but there are so many features that are super basic, crucial and intuitive that if they are not fixed and/or implemented soon, I'm unsure if they will actually end up standing out between the thousands of options out there.

I hope the developers can take this constructive feedback and improve the app as soon as possible to stay relevant in this crowded space. I hope to edit or change my review in the near future. For now, I will keep using reminders given the integration with all my Apple devices and everything.

Best of luck!

title: Потрясающий дизайн с невероятно неадекватным ИИ
body:
Начну с хорошего - дизайн приложения. Все :) 

А теперь что тут не так: 
- Удалят теги нельзя 
- Создавать свои списки задач нельзя 
- Коммуникация идет через Ии который иногда очень странно или супер поверхностно додумывает за тебя подзадачи, сами задачи, сам определяет приоритет и ставит эмодзи (отключить любимый Ии конечно нельзя))
- Разделение на утро/вечер/ночь 

Я могу долго перечислять но если коротко: приложение ставит тебя в рамки как ты должен им пользоваться, а если тебе это неудобно, не нужно и наоборот больше путает - терпи. Старые напоминалки по-прежнему остаются самым классным приложением для задач. 

А и еще - у тебя не будут сразу пропадать все задачи сразу же как что-то случается с интернетом и плавность порой сильно хромает

title: Good except for one flaw
body:
It’s a good app. It makes sense. The Open Ai reskinning is kind of gimmicky but that’s what people are excited about. 

The HUGE, and I cannot understate, HUGE issue and annoyance is that you can’t simply drag and drop to dos into other lists. It’s infuriating. All I want to do is pick up “workout” and drag it from morning to afternoon. 

Instead, you have to open each item and manually select which grouping it sits under. Such a hilariously simple flaw on an otherwise good thing. With respect, I mean c’mon team. iPhone Apps have been teaching us to use that touch feature for almost 20 years…

UPDATED:

Upon further use over the course of a week, this app unnecessarily complicates what Apple gets right with the simple, humble to do.

Save yourself $60 a year and just make a manual todo list with (Morning/ Day/ Evening) separations. 

This app is actually quite poorly designed in its over complication, and their support team is slow to respond, even when they’re online. 

Congratulations on a good cash grab ladies.

title: Not for busy people or long term planning. Might be good for teens?

I need to manage collections of tasks and translate those collections into meaningful time blocks, sometimes spread over multiple days sometimes over multiple months. The app, however, appears designed for users with schedules consisting of isolated, low-stakes items rather than for structuring even modestly complex workloads. Might be a great way for teens to learn how to schedule? Not sure how a working professional is supposed to use this.

title: Great idea, poor implementation
body:
The idea of this app is great. It combines your todo list and calendar in one. It also displays your todo list in a much more manageable way. The basic notifications work well.

The app falls apart quickly once you start to use its core features. The AI assistant is somehow overkill for such a simple app, and useless at doing basic things. I’ve had it spout nonsense to me after asking it to create a basic task. The AI also requires a constant connection and takes a few seconds for each request. That’s not great for an app where I need to jot down basic thoughts as fast as possible.

The lock screen and Home Screen widgets technically work. But once you have more than the allotted 5 todos that it can show, you will realize it’s just choosing random items. I’ve had it stuck on showing the last todo of my day for some time now. That’s useless when I need to do know what to do more immediately.

I know it’s nitpicking but the creepy face in the app icon and AI is off-putting. I actively don’t want to click on it.

I know it’s difficult but I would I would appreciate a better connection between the Reminders app and Tiimo. As of now, all Tiimo can do is show an Apple icon next to todos from Reminders. But they lack most of the features of a Tiimo todo.

Also no macOS app. That’s an instant thumbs down for me. The web app doesn’t automatically sync with the calendar like the iOS app does. So the web app isn’t a great alternative to the macOS app.

And no Siri integration. Which is one of the quickest/easiest ways for me jot down todos. If the app worked with Reminders better, this might not be an issue.

title: Extremely frustrating and useless
body:
It's been a long time since I hated an app this much. During the set-up it asks me my main goal, I say I want stronger routines. So it asks me what I do during my morning, day, evening, etc, using premade options, and then spits out a completely useless schedule for things I don't need help doing, like drinking coffee or taking breaks. And those are forecasted forever into the future. There are tons of them.

Okay, that was an annoying waste of time, but it gets much worse. YOU CANNOT DELETE THESE ROUTINES  EASILY. You can't just swipe and get options to get rid of them, neither temporarily or permanently. There does not seem to be a list or setting somewhere to edit it, or if there is, it's not intuitive to find it. So what do you have to do?

YOU HAVE TO MANUALLY TYPE OUT INSTRUCTIONS TO THE AI TO DELETE THE ROUTINES. AND THEN IT DOESN'T, REALLY. LOL. You tell it to delete all the routines, it says it does but doesn't. You ask it again and it might decide it can delete more, but eventually it claims there aren't any when almost all of them are left.

So I have a useless app full of trash tasks I can't delete, just within minutes of first opening it.

Also, this is less significant but I absolutely hated the "are you neurodivergent?" question in the set-up. Who cares? The term means nothing anymore, and if it means something, it means something wildly different for everyone who answers it. Someone with ADHD is not the same as someone with autism, and savants are different still, etc. Grouping all those together for no reason, as if this app could do anything very different about any of those (especially with no specifics!), was absurd and made me cringe.

title: High potential but very frustrating
body:
This app looks potentially great, but In having several frustrations:

2. You can’t create sub tasks unless you subscribe, which seems like a bit of an unnecessary feature to keep behind a paywall.
3. There’s no free trial, so I can’t test out any of the interesting advanced features to see if they would actually be helpful or not.
4. The cost is $54 / year or a whopping $12/ month (for reference, TickTick is an amazing app that costs just $35.99 yearly or $3.99 / month, and most other great to-do list apps are in a similar range). Without getting to even test out the advanced features, I see no reason to buy this app or any reason why this price tag could be worth it.

body:

- iPad app is a big version of the iPhone app. There’s a web app that is far more featured, and no real reason why the native iPad app can’t implement the web app view. 

- so when I try to use the web app on iPad, it just doesn’t load. I’m stuck at the login screen. 

- reordering tasks on the web app is painful. It’s so finicky as to be frustrating and makes me not want to do it. 

- copying tasks (things I need to do multiple times a day) causes the time to complete them to change at random 

I love what y’all are doing but these things are blockers for me potentially. Fix the iPad app and I think I’ll be able to update my rating.

body: This app is almost perfect and I have tried every single planning app on the App Store. I do not exaggerate. I swear I have had this in my head for years hoping someone would design it. And that is being able to sort my tasks by tag or category. Only being able to sort them by priority doesn’t work great for my particular neurodivergent brain. Right now I’m having to use reminders to categorize all of my tasks and then move my tasks just for the next couple of days into the tiimo app, which is not ideal. title: Love the app, BUT…
body:
I truly love this app. Of all the to-do list apps I’ve used (and I’ve used most all the major ones!) this is my favorite. However, there’s a glowing flaw that, as an ADHDr, boggles my mind. You cannot bulk select tasks from a previous day and move them to the next day. There is an evening check-in that allows this, but if you miss it, you’re screwed and you have to go through and manually change the date on EACH AND EVERY TASK. Not only that, but they do not default to the “To-do” section. So all these not done tasks just float in their respective days where you had good intentions of completing them until you either move them manually or just throw your hands in the air and say screw them. 🤷🏼‍♀️

This will be a dealbreaker for me on this app if it not fixed soon. I need things to roll to the next day in bulk because I’m not always in a position to do the evening check-in when it pops up. And, as an ADHDr, I FORGET! 

PLEASE PLEASE FIX THIS.
author: Gloriously distracted

title: Close to wonderful
body:
Timo is exactly the app I was looking for. It was clearly made for people whose brains work like mine. I TRY to use it every day, all day to keep myself on task, moving between my home life tasks and my work life tasks. The problem is that the app is not reliable. It regular has glitches that keep me from being able to add or edit a task. I get the spinning wheel of death a lot. The integration 
with Google and outlook calendars was exactly the right idea, but that too is unreliable. It often takes hours for Timo to show an event that’s been added to the Google calendar, and I’ve never been able to successfully integrate my outlook calendar from work. Please keep working on this app — it’s the best thing I’ve found for ADHD task management, it just needs some work to feel worth the money and effort to use it.
author: JZM7568

title: Great structure and UX but performance could use improvement
body: I absolutely love using Tiimo! It is such a great take on task management and planning for an ADHDer like myself. It is just the right balance of structure, encouragement, nudging, and forgiveness (not shoving missed tasks in your face) to help you stay on top of things. There are also some great instructor led course for various things helpful for someone who is neurodivergent. My favorites so far have been “Make budgeting ADHD-friendly” and “Leading as an ADHD’er”. The only negative I have at the moment is that the performance of the app can be a bit slow at times. Particularly when saving changes to tasks. I would imagine that will get better with time though.

title: Disappointed in the recent updates
body:
I used to love this app, but recent updates have made it less productive and harder to use :(
This is no longer an “ADHD Task & Planning Assistant” like the description entails. It’s become a time-waster for people with ADHD.

This makes me so sad because I’ve been using the app for a year and a half and as an ADHD person it really helped me manage my time. But now it’s become too difficult and distracting trying to work around the new “features” and bugs. 

We can no longer time tasks by minute, but now only by 5 min intervals.
Sometimes when I add tasks they get added to the next day instead of the current day and I have to go searching for them.
There’s no longer an option for pre-made routines.
When I’m changing and moving around my tasks they don’t update automatically and I have to close out and reopen the app in order for them to update.
The new AI options are unnecessary and get in the way.

I’m really hoping you read through the reviews and feedback and change the app for the better.

Persistent notification in dynamic island and the watch complication both dont work anymore. When I want to be productive, these were there to keep me reminded of what I was supposed to be doing.

Now I have to open the app and next thing you know I’m distracted again. 

Great design, concept and positioning. But flawed to a point of being unusable.

title: Ohhh how I wish I could get my money back!!!
body:
I don’t need a fresh new glow up, or a new icon. I don’t need AI task management. 
I DO NEED the app to load when I open it on the first try. And I really need those features that made this app so awesome that I decided to purchase a lifetime membership. The routines, the ability to set a duration of time and then set the end time and the app would automatically set the start time. THAT is precisely what my neurodivergent brain NEEDS and that is exactly what I paid for. But it was taken away I keep waiting for them to bring it back but instead they keep adding things that I don’t need. I don’t need to see HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW on the To-Do list. Or at least give the ability to turn those off, it’s very distracting. 
Ohhh, and I doesn’t sync across devices, you have to load each calendar for each device. 
The only thing I use is the Focus Timer so I can visually see how much time I have left (mostly getting ready to go somewhere) and this only works if I’ve done the math correctly to begin with because that’s one of the features that were taken away. Ohhh how I wish I could get my money back!!! 

My previous review Aug 10, 2025:
DON’T WASTE YOUR MONEY!!! 

It’s been a little over three months since I wrote my original review and nothing has improved. I am beyond frustrated because this app no longer has the features that made me decide to fork over $59! I don’t need or want AI, I want to be able to plan my day with routines (no longer a feature) and to reverse plan my day (also no longer available). They say they’re “committed to supporting executive functioning and daily planning in the best possible way” but all I see them committed to is taking people’s money. And yes, there is a weekly/monthly overview on the web planner but it only shows events that are directly in your iCal or Google calendar, and if you are subscribed to other calendars, they don’t show up on the web planner. So the web planner is basically useless. Bottom line; DON’T WASTE YOUR MONEY!!!

My previous review May 6, 2025:
Used to be perfect, now it’s just a mess.

Well, close to perfect. I paid the lifetime fee for this app and I wasted my money! I used to be able to do reverse scheduling; my appointment is at 1:15, I like to give myself 15 minutes arrival time to park and get inside so I would set the task for 15 min duration and the end time for 1:25 and the app would automatically set the start time. Same for travel time, 40 minutes to get there, set duration then the end time and app would set the start time. I’d plan my whole day this way. BUT now this feature is no longer there. I have to do the time math myself and if I’m wrong I could be late. I love the visual timer but it’s useless to me if I’m not on time. The main reason I purchased this VERY EXPENSIVE app was for the task duration and ability to plan my day backwards. 

There are many more features that would improve this app like the ability to glance at the week, or drag/drop multiple tasks when an appointment gets rescheduled, the ability to leave a comment (not a note) in the task, but I could (and did) live without these things. HOWEVER, I NEED the task duration returned!!!!

I don’t understand WHY features that were there when we PAID for the app would be removed.

title: Please allow tasks without emojis + fix cross-device syncing outside of the Apple Ecosystem
body:

1) I can’t remove emojis from tasks, even when I delete them, they still show up. 

2) The AI support tool also forces emojis, even when I explicitly ask it not to.

title: It's not a Planner. Makes me feel MORE disabled.
body:
Tiimo has some good stuff.  
I haven't used the app for months because I was so put off by the frustrating bugs when tried to add monthly bills.  

Today I realized that I really want to try to use an iPad/iPhone app for my primary calendar instead of a paper one...  and it seems that tiimo ios doesnt have a week or month view.  Only the desktop version has month view.  This doesn't make sense.  For an app that costs money and has SO MANY extra features, even courses... the absence of something so essential to planning makes me feel like I must not be human or have once again slipped into a dystopian universe.                       I can't confidently set daily goals in the morning or review and re-plan at the end of the day without seeing long term views!  Like how can anyone?  									I have a great visual memory, but apparently this app is made for you the majority who can memorize and visualize all your long term goals, tasks, and events/appointments to the point you don't need to view them when daily planning and working.  												 
September 24:    complete failure on first attempt to set up.
I just updated to ios 18.1 and it will NOT save items i set to repeat on a monthly date (such as bills).  I've tried multiple times and they keep resetting to "today / anytime"   It's be.  Truly bizarre.   

ALSO:  There NEEDS to be a place to view different tasks/ events as chronological lists.    

Even in the first days of Apple and Google calandars you can click and unclick which categories we want to see show up - so we can choose to view everything in a list or on a monthly or weekly calendar   or we can view different combinations of these subcategories :  
a. daily repeating / anytime tasks    
b. monthly tasks  
c.  one time tasks         
It's so MADDENING to see all these crandom events cluttering up my tasks from facebook or google, including acquatinance birthdays or community events I'm not interested in.   You can't click on them to make them go away!
Come on now.  This is basic planner type stuff!   If this doesn't get fixed in the next 3 days, I'm going to need a refund, because this app will be completely worthless to me.  I need something that can do all these things, otherwise I might as well just have a bunch of different free apps that only do parts of these things.

author: Jacob A Norris

title: Overall, I’m a FAN!
body:
UPDATED:
Tiimo developers seem to be continually listening and adjusting the app based on feedback, which is very much appreciated. The updates have made planning much easier, and my timers are now synched. SUPER happy that my page now immediately opens to the planning vs the learn section. I am OK with the routines being gone now since I find the suggestions for “self-care” even better because what is offered is great and I can easily customize. I am still hoping options for a palette come out but it’s fine. I am a fan of this app and will continue to pay for the learn portion, too. It’s always great to have resources to understand more about how brains work! 

PREVIOUS:

I am willing to invest in an app to keep myself on task and organized. While I didn’t want to pay right away, I got an offer (that would shortly expire) for 25% off so took the leap after playing with it for a day. I am already frustrated. If I schedule a task, like a meeting, but then the meeting runs over…that will affect the rest of my plans. This happened today. But once the Tiimo time starts, it’s VERY difficult to readjust the other tasks. I knew there (unfortunately) wasn’t an easy way to batch-shift all tasks to a new time (say, move them all 15 minutes), but I was willing to adjust each one. The problem is, again, once the timer starts. My only choices are to resume or pause the task. Pausing it makes it look gray as though I have completed it. Editing it does NOTHING, inexplicably. The only surefire way is to delete the task and start all over again—how is this effective for saving mental energy and time?

Also, it would be really helpful if there was a way to select colors and create our own palette that could be used consistently and easily. While there is a way to save colors, it’s clunky to get to them.

I also read that there is a way to create routines but either that’s gone now or it’s just not intuitive for me.

I used this app every day to help organize my schedule. The color coding helped a lot, as well as adding sub-tasks. Everything changed when AI was added. Now it automatically tries to fill in the icon and color for each activity you add. Going in and changing it adds a layer of friction that became too much since I had so many things to put. Small changes all over the app have occurred since then that makes it more complicated to add items, or to keep them matching up with whatever system I try and establish.

It would be one thing if the AI could be turned off, but that’s just not possible in the current form. I want to be able to use this app without problem, it was an essential tool for nearly the whole time I had it. I just can’t in it’s current state.

title: TERRIBLE UPDATE REMOVED ROUTINES
body:

title: Beautiful Design, But Fails on Functionality
body:
Tiimo has a stunning interface and a calming aesthetic, but unfortunately, that’s not enough. The routines feature is completely missing, which is baffling given the app's purpose. Without routines or the ability to include subtasks with custom times, the app falls short of supporting those with executive functioning challenges — the very group it's marketed to help.
As it stands, Google Calendar combined with Google Tasks does a better job at planning and structure — and it’s free. Tiimo feels like a premium wrapper around features that are either missing or half-implemented. It’s a nice idea, but without the fundamentals, it doesn’t deliver where it matters most.

title: 🚀Life changing for neurodivergent people‼️
body:
Tiimo is for us, neurodivergent people; since trying it 2 months ago, the way my days go is different. I’m happier and more confident ; the level of executive functioning I’m able to muster + tasks I’m able to get done is remarkable in comparison to beforehand… and again, it’s done so much for my self esteem. Because I’ve always had so many ideas and goals but never can execute them due to my ADHD…d I’ve tried EVERY paper planner & planner app under the sun, and nothing works after the initial dopamine of a new system wears off… the tool becomes another task….. But Tiimo is so obviously designed by us and for us, neurodivergent friends! 

It not only is the first system to stick for me , but  it also actually helps me not only be more productive but have an overall higher QOL — thank you for finally making our people an app that’s a real TOOL — I feel like for the first time I can finally use my ADHD super powers to my advantage . 

The app features are great and unique (truly the timer…..a stroke of genius that could only be from a neurodivergent brain ) , but I also equally love the community sense from the app… ADHD makes follow-through so hard, and so many of us are so hard on ourselves and suffering in silence — this app’s got a built in neurodivergent community to help me be accountable. From the music live sessions to the courses on and designed for being productive within our neurodivergence make me feel supported ! I Can’t recommend this enough to everyone with ADHD — if you wanna know , finally, what it feels like to be productive consistently via a tool / system that’s implemented so easily , this is a must. The paid subscription is also so cheap …. Worth it!

title: Great idea, poor web app execution

I almost wish they didn’t provide the sync so it wasn’t so confusing. It does not handle multiple events well (I was making dinner and also working while the food was in the oven). And if a task takes longer than expected I can’t go back and change it or add more time? I wish that when a task ended instead of saying “great job!” it started counting UP to show you how much time you’re now OVER your predicted time allotment. I wanted to leave a review bc I really like this app, but it’s unusable for me the way it is, so I hope some great improvements are made (native desktop??) so it can be even better.

title: Highly Disappointed
body: I was quite excited to try this app to help stay on task throughout the day and battle ADHD symptoms. But after using it for about a week, I couldn’t be more disappointed. It’s a fairly well-polished app and looks beautiful, but form seemed chosen over function. For example, there is no way to snooze a task or have it roll into the following day if it goes incomplete for the day; so I had to go backwards and reschedule all of the incomplete tasks for new dates. This was not ideal for someone with ADHD. It’s too easy to forget tasks as it is, and the app simply started a new day with a blank slate rather than addressing the ones that were incomplete from the day before. I couldn’t understand the lack of features so I tried the pro subscription. There was no free trial offered, but I took a risk to give the app more of a chance. The risk did not pay off, and now Apple is refusing to refund me for a year’s subscription after only using the app for less than a week. Tiimo also made the timer feature a prime function, but it was rather buggy and unreliable. Additionally, tasks that were scheduled for a time would automatically start a timer at that time whether I wanted it to or not. This didn’t make sense to me and I’d often felt rushed into a task that I was not ready for. It was like the app would punish you for being late to start something scheduled. I think Tiimo would work well for a lot of people, but not for me. And I don’t understand why I wasn’t given a free trial. Now I am out $41 for an app that I no longer use.

author: Funphone(:! 321

title: This App Changed My Life
body: I can’t express what Tiimo is to me as an app and the degree to which it has changed my life. I encourage every neurodivergent person I know to try it. I have struggled my entire life with time blindness and staying current with my self care routines. I am a person who desperately needs routines to function but has trouble maintaining them. I built my routines into the app and add them to my schedule daily and it helps me figure out more than any other tool I’ve tried how to carve out that time for myself. I also am able to create much more realistic goals for myself because it forces me to think about how much time things actually take. Setting realistic goals and not over scheduling myself has lead to a greater sense of accomplishment that in turn encourages me to accomplish more. I also have been more on time to things than I have ever been. I end every day with the review function and plan out the next day. It helps me so much with the paralysis I’ve always felt when deciding what to do and what is most important to prioritize. Also, this app is created by the most incredible team. They are not just pumping this app out here- they legitimately deeply care about their mission to create a productivity app for neurodivergent people. I heard about an upcoming feature change that I used heavily and was concerned. I sent them a loooong email not expecting to hear back. They not only responded but helped me to understand the change and work through what it would mean for me. They went above and beyond to help me feel comfortable (because as we know, neurodivergent people can struggle with change.) They are ALWAYS there to help when you need assistance with the app and they do so with genuine compassion, care, and kindness.
author: ashleyback

title: Just liars & thieves taking advantage of ADHD impulsivity.
body: This is definitely not an ADHD friendly app!  They lie about features and ease of use to take advantage of ADHD impulsivity. You read their lies and pay for features then find out the truth. I do believe that every person building this app has ADHD & zero communication skills across their teams. Searching for specific instructions is not an option, there is NO search bar. And the “Create a master routine in the routine library” (routine library) doesn’t exist! The whole reason I paid for this app for a year! Features aren’t consistent between iOS devices, much less the web/browser. You can’t add an end date when setting up a repeating task. After adding the task you can go find what needs to be the last one and delete all future. How is that ADHD friendly? The “custom repeat” is not custom!  I use a medication every 3 days but I can’t set that up with one task. NOT ADHD FRIENDLY!!! I could go on but you get the idea.

author: Kate9210

title: The app that helped change my life
body:
I didn’t think that any productivity app could help put me on a path that would lead to my dreams coming true. Yet the techniques and lessons I learned from using Tiimo have helped me to build the skills in such a way that I now do most thing out of habit and need the app less and less. 

That right there is pure magic and should be the point of all apps that are focused on helping people become more organized and especially when they are designed as thoughtfully as Tiimo; with the neurodivergent community in mind. Don’t miss out on the videos and how to tools in the app as they can really teach you things you thought you knew but really could benefit from learning more about. 

I found myself more successful in using Tiimo due to some of the quality of life perks such as the ability to utilize colors and emojis in interface that make it easier for my brain to sort and process the information it is seeing.

It’s essential features like this that help set Tiimo apart from the rest. I also very much appreciate the ability to have multiple profiles. As someone with multiple disabilities and varying needs in my day to day life, I value being able to switch profiles so that I can access different sets of daily tasks.

Not every productivity or organizational app is for everyone, but the flexibility provided by Tiimo means that I’m confident you’ll find something beneficial from giving it a download and trial run. Good luck and enjoy your Adventures in the Apple App Store!

You have to KNOW you didn’t complete something to reschedule it. Unfinished tasks should just roll over or at least be turned into todo items. 

Stuff like that makes me wonder if this app was truly made with ADHD people in mind. I wanted this to work out. I downloaded after hearing the ad on a podcast. (NO DISCOUNT CODE by the way.) But nah this ain’t for me. I’ll be trying other apps after this.

title: Navigating the app is difficult for me.
body:
I have ADHD and this app is driving me crazy so far. I’ve only tried it a couple of times, but I can’t even figure out how to delete a recurring event because I don’t want it there. 

The interface doesn’t work intuitively with iOS. You can’t swipe to delete, and it’s not easy to work the app when you first use it. The tutorials I found were videos, which I have a hard time with. I’d rather be walked through each step with a tutorial I can try as I’m learning. And having a help/FAQ section that functions like an indexed instruction manual would be even more 

It seems to me that basic things are too complicated in this app. Extra steps drive me nuts. 

EDIT: customer service got back to me and showed me how to delete apps. That really helped and I’ve been using the app for the last couple of days. 

I still think there are too many steps to jump in and do basic things, and I find myself skipping the reminders I’ve set up. I’m an educated person, but I’m still having trouble navigating and easily finding the features I want to use.

author: Enna-chan

title: Niche. Not for me
body: I feel like this app doesn’t know what it’s supposed to be. As a to do app, there’s so much friction in adding actual tasks. Compared to other to do apps, it takes more taps to add and modify tasks. There’s no natural language parsing. And it lags. As a scheduler, it fails to take into account that rarely does a day go according to plan. You can’t reschedule easily or auto schedule. The focus function is bare bones. As a mood tracker, there are other apps that consolidate and track the metric more insightfully, like being able to draw correlations or directing you to CBT methods. As a calendar, where is two way sync? I think Tiimo tries to do a lot of things, but none of them are executed particularly well. Despite the pretty UI, the functionality isn’t smooth. The web app does show potential—it feels much better to time block on there than in app.

title: Lifetime Purchase, Lifelong Disappointment—Bring Back Routines!
body:
I am one of the loyal users who bought Tiimo outright when the lifetime purchase was an option. I invested in Tiimo specifically for the routines feature, which was a lifeline for my daily structure and productivity. Having ADHD, routines aren’t just a preference—they’re essential. I relied on this app for the flexibility to check off tasks and smoothly switch through routines without a second thought. It was like having a supportive, invisible coach guiding me through my day.

Now, with routines gone, I’m left with a “task with subtasks” workaround that doesn’t switch properly and lacks the seamless flow that routines offered. What am I supposed to do with a ‘lifetime’ app that no longer fulfills its primary function?

Removing such a core feature feels like breaking a promise to those of us who paid for the app as it was. I’d gladly pay a bit extra if that’s what it takes to bring routines back as an add-on, but don’t take away something that was a dealbreaker for so many users. Please reconsider this change, or at least give us a roadmap on whether there’s any hope for a feature revival.

author: Ned cannonmenace

title: The perfect app… until they got rid of routines
body: After years of medical mysteries, I finally got an accurate diagnosis and treatment for an otherwise debilitating sleep disorder. For the first time in my adult life, I realized I could go to college, but I knew I would need help, so I poured myself into researching assistive technologies that could help me manage my day-to-day activities and routines as I adapted to the new experience of college life. I heard so many good things about Tiimo - it kept coming up over and over again in my research, so once I got my new iPad, I purchased the subscription and dedicated myself to learning how to use it. Now, I am a 4.0 student, an orientation leader, and an advocate for my fellow students with disabilities. It's amazing what the right diagnosis, treatment, and assistive technologies can do to level the playing field - I am finally competing with my peers after years of feeling like I could never measure up. I barely graduated high school, but now, I'm the top of my class at my local university. Having a set and scheduled routine is such a big thing for me. A big part of my morning challenges is mental fatigue - I just literally don't have the ability in the mornings to do the mental math and prioritization to quickly figure out on the fly what I need to change if something goes awry. The way the routines feature managed my time and the granularity of the subtasks within each timed activity had been such an absolute game changer for me. I literally cut an hour out of my morning routine once I started using Tiimo because I wasn’t wasting time trying to recalibrate after each activity. This is my biggest executive function deficit and the way this feature just smoothed it right over and allowed me to truly function at full capacity was such a big deal to me. The hours of developing and redeveloping these routines as my needs changed over time were all rendered null and void when the Tiimo team got rid of the routine function (which individually timed each activity in the routine and automatically removed that time from the greater routine) and gave us… One activity with untimed subtasks? Now, instead of being able to see how much time I have left in my routine to know if I’ll be able to catch the bus at a glance, I need to get a calculator out on my phone to see if it would be a waste of time to eat breakfast or not. Additionally, several of my routines were long, with around 20 activities, some of which had subtasks to them, so now, I have to scroll up and down the subtasks list of around 30 items on what used to be a simple routine. The loss of the routines function was hard enough, but the solution you implemented, having subtasks that just lists the item of the routine and the time it takes was also impacted in a recent update that makes checking off those items even harder. I spent ten minutes tonight trying to figure out how to view and check off subtasks from the day menu, only to find that to check off a subtask, you now have to go into the edit menu, check off the subtask, and save it to make sure the items stay checked. Before the update, this was simple and straightforward, but now I have to expend mental energy that I do not have to go through this elongated process, just to check something off of a list. Even worse - the reasoning for the removal of the routines function comes off as incredibly ableist and snarky. I may be one of "only" 300 paying users to utilize the routines function, but I am a paying user and the features that keep me as a Tiimo user are still important! At least give me the option to opt in to a more deluxe membership - I'd gladly pay a few more dollars a month for a feature that has become so critical to my success! I understand that software companies right now are struggling, but is the only option to remove one of the most important features from a paying user? Because what's left isn't enough to maintain my membership.

author: courtneyxxjane

title: I’m done
body:
I’ve been using this app for ages, and happily paying for it, and Routines is why. It was the one thing that made it ideal for me over other apps (and was so useful to me that it made up for the glitches and other design frustrations). Now Routines have been “simplified” to the point of no longer being useable, as the developers want to make a generic AI list-generator app instead (I already have one, thanks, and it’s one that works better and is much less expensive than this).

Silver lining is I need a new phone anyways, so this is an opportunity to drop some apps like Tiimo that are dead weight and save big on my app subscription costs. I appreciated the convenience of an app that did what Tiimo used to do and I hope some other app is out there that actually cares about the needs of their userbase (see: Tiimo’s predatory subscription model + the fact that they specifically target disabled users for their product. Not a good look!). But worst case, I can replicate Routines with a checklist app and a timer, which seems to fly in the face of their claim that it’s “to hard” to continue to update the feature that sold me on the product in the first place. 

Tiimo, your marketing doesn’t make up for a bad product, even when your target demographic is more vulnerable than most. And lot of us have more time on our hands than you do and we *will* spread the word.
author: Lizzylearnsfrench

title: Do Not Like the Oct 2024 Update
body:
Unless I am missing something, after the update, it does not appear that there is a timer for the individual tasks in a routine. One overall timer for the entire routine is not helpful. I want to know how much time I’m spending on each task, to ensure that I’m on track to finish my routine in the desired amount of time. If I wanted one overall timer, I could just use the built in timer on my phone for free. Additionally, it does not appear that there is a setting that can be changed for the “Anytime” category to appear at the top, instead of “Planned.” And the perpetual “Schedule a Virtual Focus Session” button blocks the view of the task that is displayed behind it when a routine is running.

Previous Review 3 Stars - Inability to Not Import All-Day Events is Disappointing: I frequently use all-day events as reminders (bill due dates, dog’s monthly medication, and future date events that I cannot schedule yet) so on any given day I can have at least 5 - 6 all-day events. Perhaps I’m in the minority, but since I have many other apps that allow me to exclude all-day events, I’m very shocked that this isn’t an option with this app. It discourages me from using the timer because I have several concurrent timers going, and the list of all-day events takes up a decent amount of space in the calendar view. It appears that there is a planned update for this, so I hope that it occurs soon because this feature is really impacting my user experience.

author: Bill The Man #2

title: An app for ADHD…disgraceful
body:
I tried this for a day and it was not what I was hoping it would be and turned it off. Of course I get a charge for the highest annual subscription two days ago. 

A courtesy email reminder “hey, your trial period is ending in 2 days, please cancel or choose a plan, otherwise you’ll be penalized with the highest annual plan” wouldn’t be that difficult. 

That’s not good business,  ESPECIALLY considering the market you are targeting. I’m quite aware NOW that there is a small place that says you’ll be billed if you don’t cancel so my mistake, but the appearance is that us forgetting is what you’re banking on, taking advantage of the most vulnerable prey. Annual too, that’s just wrong. 

The app may work for some, but it was a hindrance to me. The “do anytime” was a complete waste but the worst part is when something comes up or you’re in a zone and not ready to stop something, it pauses but continues on so the next several tasks just kept on coming, no asking how much more time do you need to rearrange the schedule but it pauses but continues on with the next thing like you can do 5 things at once. It was way more work and caused more chaos than it was worth in my case. 

I’ve turned all notifications off again and will delete the app that you decided I wanted for a whole year.

Unsolicited business advice, but the appearance is shady and in the age of social media, appearances are everything. This could be handled way better and show some kindness to those who are already struggling.

author: OhSnowUdidnt

title: Useful but buggy…
body:
I got this app because I needed help visualizing time. I had a bad habit of always running late and wanted to get to work earlier than I was doing before. So far, it’s helped in that regard once I fine tuned my schedule and I consistently used it in the weekdays. While I’m disappointed that manually making checklists is behind a paywall, I still find the premade ones helpful and it’s helped me get through my workdays. But the reason I docked a star is because it’s so buggy in the one area I really need it: the visual timer. 

If I pause the timer on the Home Screen of my phone, there’s a 50% chance it doesn’t actually register and the clock is still running in the app, or I tell it to resume and doesn’t start in the app. This is immensely frustrating, because if I go in the app to check something off and to see how much time I have left, there’s a chance the clock never even started again! Or the timer will say I have one minute left on the home screen but then six minutes in the app. This throws me and my schedule in the app off. How am I supposed to visualize time if the app can’t even keep time too? 😭 I’ll still use the free version but I won’t pay for it until this is fixed.

title: No free version
body: The app description here includes this: “PRICE & GENERAL TERMS Timo offers two auto-renewing membership options. […] Timo offers a free version of the app, which gives access to basic planning features.” There is no free version; there is a 7-day free trial when you sign up for a subscription. That’s not a free version, that’s a temporary free trial that’s only free if you remember to cancel it on time. For an app that purports to be designed especially for the neurodivergent crowd - we who notoriously lose track of things - that seems either completely clueless, or bordering on the criminal.
