author: mrmckevin

title: Subscription models are predatory
body:
This app has so much potential but if you’re experimenting with the free version, even the tutorial constantly has you click things that bring up the “NO YOU MUST SUBSCRIBE TO BREAK DOWN A TASK”. 
A subscription model specifically being targeted at neurodivergent people takes advantage of them forgetting small monthly charges and bumps prices later. Its designed to have an gratifying flow to set it up, and then will break flow repeatedly in ways that will annoy vulnerable people into a quick sub. Then it does the bait and switch of “try for $3/mo or save with $36 a year in advance.” This is an advertising tactic that works really well on impulsive people, particularly those suffering from a mental health crisis. 
I would happily pay $10 one time for this app after a testing period of a few days. But I’m not giving money to intentionally exploitative subscription models.

title: Still has issues.
body:
I like this app, it provides a lot more flexibility and features than most planner apps. Great options for taggings, colors, and icons. But in other ways, the app is too unreliable and distracting. 
UI has issues on an older iphone SE with a smaller screen. Some menus are slightly cut off at the bottom of the screen. I also wish that most menus let you see more tasks on screen, I feel like this app often takes too much scrolling. 
Too many popup ads for random events and features I don’t care about, even though I pay for a subscription. I need a planner app. Your blogposts and classes are extra distractions that I don’t need, and the app gives no option to disable those popups. 
Widgets, notifications, and watch app are convenient but unreliable, especially if you don’t open the app frequently. It’s still nice to have, but it makes it just a bit harder to justify the subscription fee.

title: Beware of these people.
body:
I tried to step out for one day. Just one day. I clicked the free trial button and very next day I decided the app was not for me and I went to cancel the trial only to find they charged me for an entire entire year subscription.  I reached out to them about this they refused to return my money. They claimed that I had also tried to free trial this app in 2020. Hello! I have ADHD! I don’t remember that. And even if it did happen, it makes no sense to me that my punishment for accidentally re-downloading the same app twice in 5 years is a $45 charge. Are you useless than 24 hours of this service. 

I warn you against doing any business with people who have such shady practices. As for the app itself, I feel like I was a victim of hype from various ADHD influencers. It’s just another task management app. Nothing life-changing.

 I prefer to use Structured. It makes more sense. And it’s much much cheaper at only $15 a year. It has a web app. Tasks that take different amount of times are  diffeeent sizes and you can set an energy budget so you know how much tasks take lot of you. 

As for Tiimo, I don’t think the way that you add task is very intuitive. There is also no way to add a multi step routine each day. The AI task breakdown is nice, but structured also has that feature. For for nearly $45 a year— feel cheated. Please return my money Tiimo. What you’re doing is not fair or right.

title: Wanted to like it
body:

First of all, pretty useless if you don’t pay for it. And not worth the money bc it’s stressful.
 
Personally, the app itself was super overwhelming and made me even more stressed. I didn’t even know where to start. In fact, I couldn’t even start and am deleting the app and canceling my subscription. Too complicated for an app that’s supposed to be for people with ADHD. 

You are better off using the free reminders app on your iphone and the timer on your clock app. In fact, you’re better off using notes on your iphone and making a checklist. Don’t even give this app a try.

title: Just need this one thing…
body:
The design of the app is very aesthetically appealing and easy to use. I really, really, really want to use this app on a regular basis. However, the way tasks auto start is an issue for me. If I start one task ten minutes late then my whole Tiimo schedule is messed up unless I manually pause tasks as I go. I think an easy way to fix this would be where you have the option to manually press “completed task” when you’re done and *then* it automatically moves to the next task after this. If you haven’t finished the task yet but you’re over the time limit you set for it, your next tasks just sit there waiting and don’t start until you’re done with this one. This way there’s no breaks in the routine but your whole schedule isn’t messed up if you’re a few minutes late.

Please Tiimo, let me know if you plan on doing something about this soon. Like I said I really want to use Tiimo but for the meantime I think I will have to use a different app.

title: Paying to be reminded on a reminding app!?
body:
Do not get me wrong. Tiimo WAS a fantastic apps before this update; it was free to create a checklist and have widgets on your iOS device, but now it is basically useless.

 I stopped using Tiimo briefly after starting school because everyone has their own schedule, but I started using it again this summer because I have all the time in the world and need to keep track of it because of my neurodivergence and OH BOY. The first thing I saw was a subscription ad, which is fine since the app is still fictional without the extra abilities, right? WRONG. Apparently, if you want to create a checklist to meet your particular needs or if you want to be reminded before you activity, you must pay. 

I could understand if the membership was for other bonuses, such as virtual learning sessions or expert courses, but what about the app's overall purpose? What's the sense of having the app if it serves no function for individuals who don't have the money or who may not be able to subscribe at all? It's very aggravating; yes, the app is still usable, but it's not practical.

I would highly suggest an import function for the Reminders app that Apple has. This is the best thing about the "Structured" app. I can easily just ask Siri to add a reminder to my day while I'm driving or shopping into a specific list which will then automatically sync into the inbox on structured for me to drag and drop into a space my day or week has. 
I couldn't find an easy way to add my reminders unless I had both apps open which was just too much back and forth.
author: Krissspaaaaa

title: Needs more useful choices, less blogging
body:
Generally, I love having the app, but I’m beginning to think of exploring other options. 

***With every update, my to-do list (now called inbox??) that I took a lot of time to enter, disappears!!!

I agree with another review about your schedule just running without you whether you do it or not.  If you sleep in or something prevents you from starting the ideal schedule you pre-entered, it just starts greying out things you haven’t done and says you’re in the middle of something you haven’t started yet.  I’d rather it force ME to say - ok, begin my day now, and then proceed with the entered length of times I entered.  Or make ME tap - yes, begin this as scheduled in 5 minutes, and make ME tap that it’s done rather than just greying it out when the time is up.  If I don’t click done, it shouldn’t move on.  This should be obvious to people catering to ADHD.  The only way to kinda do this is to start and then pause, which isn’t effective.  I’m aware of rescheduling, but this isn’t really what I want to do.  

And as someone who has premium, what’s the difference between that and premium plan??  I don’t want the seminars and blogs that are now part of premium learn, that’s for sure - but it’s in my face all the time.  Stop with the fanciness and make the basic planning / schedule app that we all needed better with more setting choices and increased functionality.  Please.

body: When I saw an add for this app I thought “This is probably like the other apps and is not going to work for me.” Well, I was wrong. When I opened the app and signed up, I was confused at first. I used it for a little bit and got the hang of the basics. I planned for my day thinking I was going to forget like the other apps, but I was wrong. Something about this app made me want to care about my routine. None of the similar apps that I downloaded has done that before. The other apps give me limited things to do because I didn’t pay for a subscription, or didn’t let me do anything at all! But I like this app because of how much I can do without the subscription. I’m the type of person who procrastinates very often and is just lazy in general. So, I was surprised that this app actually worked for me and I think you should give it a try if you haven’t yet. I really like it.

author: Tzalez

title: Negative stars
body:
Don’t bother with this app, the 7 day trial is a trap!! I forgot to cancel and I asked for a refund 1 day after it was charged to my card and it wasn’t eligible for refund. I appealed the decision and after the review, they still didn’t refund me. I’m out $37 because I didn’t cancel before the trial.

They want to help people with ADHD get organized but they surely aren’t kind to them. The first thing they should teach the user is how to set a reminder to cancel before the trial period BUT setting reminders are MESSY! It preloads a “start” and “end” your day prompt that clutters the task screen. 
Pro tip: people with ADHD need as little clutter as necessary or else they will fidget with how to remove it or get distracted.

Why is the schedule messy with things we don’t need. I don’t care that I wasted money on this stupid app, I literally downloaded a free temp and did one myself. Those of you who like it for the AI assist, just plug in your task to chat gpt and ask to simplify your task or “can you put this task in bullet points?” And it will do it for you. Copy and paste onto a calendar where, when you click the day, a side note pad will show and paste that on there! You’ll more than likely remember it’s there and more likely to do it! The thing that got me was trying to reschedule tasks that I didn’t do and when I inserted the date, it wouldn’t show up on the new date. In fear I would lose that task, I just started using a post it note. 

This app is so disorganized and not helpful for people with adhd. You don’t need this app. Trust me. Don’t waste your money. 

It is a completely reasonable request to ask for a refund for a product I used for less that 10 days (and for 6, was never even opened!) and for a calendar with crappy UI. Even most stores give 30 days.

author: MUBet

title: A Lifesaver for the Neurodivergent Community
body:
Last update: add a “focus mode” that reduces clutter and I’ll be the happiest person in the world. 

Edit: I still love this app, but it’s too cluttered for me now. I understand the intent of the “Learn” tab, but it’s more stuff on the Home Screen of the app that I’ll never touch. The lofi beats are great but you hear the same track after about an hour, and that isn’t great for my focus. As someone with ADHD, the app simply has too much crammed into a space that’s suppose to help me think, not overwhelm me.

As a neurodivergent individual, Tiimo has been an absolute lifesaver for me. Having used it daily for over two years, I can confidently say it's an essential part of my routine. The app provides the structure and checklists I need to navigate my day effectively. Its AI feature is a standout, allowing me to get started quickly and’s easily on any activity. I recently used it to help me create a list to manage panic attacks. Tiimo's intuitive design and tailored approach make it unrivaled in the market. It's not just an app for me; it's a daily companion that brings order and peace to my life. I'm a loyal user for life and highly recommend it to anyone seeking a reliable, supportive organizational tool.

It also integrates seamlessly with my reminders, calendars, and other apps. 

This is the limitation of Tiimo, at least right now, in my opinion. I know it’s a work in progress so I am open to checking back in down the road.

author: Eddie Corbo

title: A waste
body:
This app had a lot of potential, to the point that I even paid the ridiculous $29.99 for a year’s subscription. It was a complete waste of money and you’re better off using iCal and something like Routinery. Here’s why:

1. The app asks to track your activity if you have iOS 17, and if you decline it will pop up and ask every time you open the app. This is so distracting if you have ADHD, for one, and two: I didn’t pay your insane price for a subscription just to get continually asked to do your marketing research for you. Fix this! It’s ugly and insulting.

2. Every time I try to add or modify a routine, there’s a 75% chance the app will crash or delete the routine.

3. No way to see if your anytime tasks will fit in your day.

4. Notifications work sporadically. I need them to give me haptic notifications on my watch and that goes through maybe 30% of the time.

5. Extremely cluttered onboarding and a ton of fancy corporate Memphis graphics but little education on how to use the app functionally. Maybe that’s because it barely functions.

Anyway, wish I hadn’t spent $30 on this so I hope I save anyone reading this some money.

author: Norywinslow

title: After Years, More Stressful Than Helpful
body:
I’ve been trying to use this app for years and stick around for the changes, but the problems have yet to be resolved. I’ve submitted these over time. I have stopped using the app for a while, hoped it’s gotten better, and returned multiple times. The restrictions on the free version have gotten terrible during that time; if I want to try the app again and see if it’s worth my time and money (that I really don’t have to begin with), I have to get the paid version to even edit older activities I’ve already set the last time I used it, even just to change the day. My complaints are the same as others and it has, overall, caused me more anxiety, stress, and grief. No refund could cover the amount of work I’ve put into using this app only for it to not function correctly. 

Examples of some problems: new activities will disappear. Ones you’ve deleted will reappear. Re-organized lists will rearrange themselves to where you’d just moved them from. The timer on your phones Lock Screen does not sync with the timer in the app if you pause or add time to it. Right now, I have given up because an activity I paused days ago is showing that it needs to be finished, despite that same activity having refreshed and started for today. I tried to update and restart, and now I have an empty activity running that won’t go away. Again, these issues haven’t been addressed and have been a problem for a very long time. 

I’m disheartened because I really want to support this app and their team; I’ve been suggesting it to others with the promises that things should be fixed up soon. I truly do not see how this app is “autistic/ADHD friendly” because all it did was take a calm organization time I had set aside for myself and made it an anxious mess that never gets cleaned up because the app can’t save itself correctly. I’m sad because I sincerely need an app like this, but I am now distrustful of the targeted neurodivergent and queer ads.

title: End up frustrated every time
body:
I really love Tiimo, I do, but the app never really seems to actually get easier to use with updates. 

There is still an issue with calendar syncing.  If you accidentally delete a calendar synced event from your timeline, you’re out of luck on ever getting it back on Tiimo.  I’ve tried un-syncing and re-syncing my calendar, signing out and back in, it never restores the event in Tiimo even though the event is still visible in my calendar.  It’s extremely frustrating to not have a fix for this, it almost eliminates the benefits of being able to sync calendars in the first place if you have to spend the extra time manually inputting things that should show up with that calendar.  Syncing across devices also still needs work..they never reflect changes made within the other. (Ex: Accidentally deleted a calendar synced event on my iPad, but it still shows up on my phone. Any edits I make will not sync across devices. So weird.)

Also, I really wish they would give us an update that has an option to have routines and events read out-loud to you.  This would be particularly helpful for your users with dyslexia, vision disabilities, etc.

title: Absolutely not for neurodivergents
body: The app is aesthetically pleasing, I’ll give it that. Aside from looking pretty, it’s nearly functionless. Way over priced and doesn’t function as advertised. As a neurodivergent, I feel like this app is not designed with my best interest in mind and the developers are just profiting from a group of people who truly need an app like this. I’ve reported issues multiple times and nothing has been fixed. 1. You can’t organize tasks. That’s right. You try to move them around and they go right back to where they started. 2. Once finished, a task stays where it is so you have to scroll through a list of completed/incomplete tasks, and like I said you can’t reorganize them. Or you can try and cross your fingers 3. Recurring tasks are limited since you can only schedule them in weekly or monthly increments. You can’t do a 10 day or 6 month recurring task. Which honestly are the hardest tasks to remember. 4. You can’t reschedule your recurring tasks. You have to send the task to another day (and if it shows up, sometimes it doesn’t) then you have to re-create the recurring task for the new day and completely delete the task and all recurring tasks from the day it was originally due. 5. Support insists you send them screenshots and videos or else they ignore the issue. 6. No task integration from other apps. A great idea for an app but executed poorly. I waste so much time trying to organize the tasks and to get it to work it defeats the purpose. I wouldn’t pay for it again and I would urge others to look elsewhere before trying to organize your life with this app. I spent so much time setting everything up it feels like such a waste. It’s just a prettier less functional version of apple tasks.

title: Good, but a beta at best
body:
Let me just say I really like the app. The creators have a page where users are able to submit features they would like to see and vote for others they’d like to see. I love this open conversation with the users. 

The app has a lot of features I really enjoy. The visual times are nice, the routines are nice. I paid for the full version to use the checklists. If you just need the visual timers and a loose plan for your day, this will work well for you. 

For me, I have severe ADHD and need to plan out even the tiniest details and be ready for last minute changes. Tiimo isn’t too great at that. Once you’ve started an activity the only way to end it is to complete it. You can let it end, and then reschedule but it’s clunky. Multiple times the timer wheel has been stuck no matter how many times I try to complete the event. 

Overall I think this project will be really great—in time. The app has lots of bugs, and a lot of features don’t work how you think they would be able to. It seems like the creators are very responsive and helpful, so I’m hoping this app will improve with time.

title: Has changed my day to day
body:
I am a paper planner girl, but this app has helped integrate technology in a way that helps me to focus. It also helps me to purposefully plan time blocks for decompressing. 

This app is so visually appealing, while also giving you some creativity in how your to do or appointment blocks appear. 

I love that my phone app calendar events are built into each day also. Another feature that is amazing is the Brain Dump log. Here you can add several thoughts, ideas, and to dos and then push them out into your schedule if it is something you want to get done. Or it stays in the Brain Dump section until you have time to look it over. There’s also the ability to reschedule something you didn’t get done. The app has built in routines (like winding down before bed) and you can also create your own. 

I highly recommend it to anyone who isn’t usually a planner because this is so different and might actually work for you.
author: Zully Hernandez

title: Great idea, poor performance
body:
I was so excited about this app when I first got it that I jumped into the premium subscription almost right away. Been using it for a little over a month and it feels like the more I use it the more I use it the worse it gets. It has so many bugs. As soon as one thing gets fixed another problem pops up. I know it can take some time to work the kinks out, but  as I understand this app has been around for a few years now, it shouldn’t feel this rough. The biggest problem I’m dealing with currently is being unable to put activities in the correct day. They always default to today! I have to mess around with it to get it to go where I intended. It’s incredibly frustrating and counter productive. Also, the lock screen timer only seems to work half the time, and there’s no rhyme or reason to it. 
Aside from the bugs, there’s other things that could make this app better. I wish it was more customizable. It would be great if the app didn’t automatically mark tasks as done just because the timer is up, and instead asked if I did the task and sent reminders until I completed it. Otherwise it’s too easy to forget to do things or leave them unfinished. I also wish I could drag the anytime items and place them in between scheduled activities so that they sit in the general portion of the day that I intend to do them. This is supposed to be a visual planner, but the way it currently stands, my tasks are all out of order. 
Anyway, I appreciate what the developers are trying to do here and I’m sure it’s not an easy task, but I just expected more, especially since I’m paying to use it and it doesn’t seem like they offer refunds.

Sadly that feature is not free. A lot of the features I was looking forward to using ended up being behind a pay wall. I also wish activities from one routine could transfer to another. It would be easier than having to make a new activity for the same thing multiple times. As well as being able to restart an activity! It's super frustrating to have to make a new activity when the app auto starts it. Its still a good app and I suggest it I just don't want others to be disappointed.

Update: Im still using the free version months later to make sure I love it and its really awesome! I love check lists and this fit all the right boxes. Seeing when my next event is has come in handy a ton! I found a work around for having to restart an activity but it takes a bit.

We need constant reminders to start a task/routine not have it assume we are doing it and also if we were diligent enough to start at time of reminder if we pause, it should have reminders to resume it cause we all know we get distracted and went to something else😉. Hope the developers can change this automatic start, I’ve went through some reviews after trying the app and realized others complain of this too. title: Has the potential to be a dream come true app
body:
As someone who seeks out customization options in every thing I own, especially apps, this app won me over. I get to upload my own icons!! Pro 1: built in timers (a rare but important habit tracking feature),   

Pro 2: customization ability 

Pro 3: tasks can be reset 

 Pro 4: widgets are well built and aesthetic.

 Con 1: timer minutes don’t keep the minutes I set them for! Such an odd bug. Support team quickly replied however and development team is on the case. But that bug is a huge problem for my personal use case. If I have a 2 minute timer, I need it to be 2 minutes. Not 1 not 4 not 12.

Con 2: apparently I never set one of my tasks as a daily. This is surprisingly easy to not set up in this app. One of the less intuitive aspects imo. As a result I missed a daily commitment and now I have to start my commitment over (it’s part of a course I’m in, and is required to do a certain amount of actions daily. Can’t miss any or I fail.) this kind of issue costs me! 

 Con 3: the videos built into this app. They NEVER go away?! AND they have a weird agenda about them too (injecting testerone???!!) please at least let us hide videos in our app, or close them out for good. Not all lifestyles are the same. And many of us with autism need a quiet app environment. Not loud visuals. 

 Overall: for many of us we pour our important tasks into apps like this. Broken features are devastating. Yet due to the potential of this app, I hope it gets some fixes.

author: Stang0767

title: Feel a bit taken advantage of, but my bad
body:
Timmo simply didn’t work for me. I have tried a couple other apps like this with the time blocking, and my main frustration is the assumption that I’m actually going to do the tasks when I have them listed.

It also simply felt clunky and needed a lot of maintenance to use throughout the day.

I am a physically disabled, neurodivergent stay at home mom. I do have several things that happen daily without fail, such as my kids’ bedtime routines, going to appointments, etc. However, as a stay at home mom, (I have 6 kids, 5 of whom are also neurodivergent) it’s up to me how my days flow. Given what kind of “mood” my ADHD is in it could be a productive, hyper-focused day, or basically the exact opposite.

The limited version of the app is available for free, however the real functionality and features are behind the paywall.

I wish I could remember exactly what it was that I was working on adding as I was attempting to set the app up after initially down loading it, but the free version had a limit of “X” number of something.

I needed more than “X” and very impulsively decided to purchase the app. I paid for the yearly subscription to save money.

It was only a matter of days until I figured out the app was not compatible with me (and I definitely think it was a compatibility issue versus Timo not being effective). Time management and productivity is very personal.

I just looked up my subscription and it expires October 19, 2023.

I did chalk this experience up to another impulsive ADHD decision that was a waste of my valuable money. However, I did decide to leave this review on April 1 (Autism acceptance month) when I saw Timmo advertising as being “Autism friendly“.

It was the “ADHD Friendly” claim that caught my eye in October 2022, (which is ADHD awareness month).

As a Neurodivergent individual, Advocate and mother of Neurodivergent kids, this personally really stung.

Neurodivergent individuals are likely more familiar than they wish with some of the common traits, including impulsivity. It’s definitely a big one for me one that has cost a significant amount of money over the years.

My boys and I are all on Social Security, and as I have said, it was my choice to pay for the app. Even if I had changed my mind the same day of the purchase (I know I stopped using I t within a few days, and tried a couple more times with no luck) it would’ve been impossible to get a refund with the subscription that I chose, and I chose the annual subscription with the intention of saving money. As we all know, paying for something we don’t use is a waste I wish Timmo would offer a free trial period of a minimum of 7 days. (I was recently given a 14-day-trial of a different app, and based on how helpful that app has been for me, I decided to purchase a six month subscription, and my decision was partly influenced by the 14-day free trial. I would not have been able to truly understand the features and benefits of the app, without access to everything that paid members receive. I’m very glad to see that this app seems to help quite a few people (based on the reviews) and you can call me sensitive, but I feel pretty creeped out by seeing an advertisement for being “autism friendly” that appeared just after midnight on the very first day of autism acceptance month. It seems very predatory to me, and the reason I am leaving this review.

2. A desktop interface for this app, either available through the macOS web store, or as a Web app.

author: Laurel💚

title: Great for sleep blindness! Not easy to adjust.
body:
* I love how the big circle shows me the passage of time as I go through my work day routines. - I have disabled my iPhone’s auto-lock so that I can keep this on my desk near my keyboard!

* I love the audible cues telling me it’s almost time to start the next task or a routine is finishing… - I’ve turned up the volume so I don’t miss that.  

* I love that I can “import” my calendar to show my appointments in line with my routines (to check for conflicts) and then un-import them so I can keep using the alerts from iPhone calendar for my appointments so I don’t confuse the audio alerts. 

But…

There are some improvements I’d like to see.  I have noticed that the help desk is responsive and it seems the developers are working hard. So…

1. I would really like the ability to turn off alerts for certain tasks.  Right now it’s all or nothing.  I would like to customize my work day routine to alert on the start of some activities, and 5 minutes before other activities, and then halfway through my longest activities.  

2. I *need* to be able to customize each type of alert.  I need to be able to recognize that a particular sound means “your activity is starting in 5 minutes” or “your activity is half over”.   Those sounds must be immediately recognizable to me or they aren’t useful; they are just noise and merely distractions.

title: So Close, Save for Bugs and Crashes
body: Tiimo is a fantastic idea of an app for those with ADHD and other neurodiverse people! But it is so incredibly buggy even with the update and it’s left me frustrated when trying to habit stack my days and structure my routines. Every time I remove a routine or calendar event, I have to restart the app to see the results or the app crashes in the process of moving events around. It’s really difficult to restart timed routines, and it can feel really defeating when you start a routine late (such as a morning routine because you needed some extra z’s) and it starts to feed to the shame cycle that all many neurodiverse people struggle with, especially time management or being behind. Even editing routine templates before inserting them into my schedule became tedious work because every little edit would take multiple tries to save it, especially checklists or descriptions under each task. It was easy to become frustrated with the app because you can see the bones of what will be a great UI interface and experience. I was really hopeful that Tiimo would be my go-to planning and task management app, but it just doesn’t clear the bar in its current iteration. It is clear how passionate the dev team is for the community it is trying to support. I am grateful for this company, and I hope they keep working on it!

author: gorogoroluv

title: Disappointed
body:
I heard about Tiimo and how it was specifically designed and developed to help neurodivergent people better organize and manage their time, days, and schedules. Being an adult who has struggled with ADD my entire life, I’m sure you can imagine how it peaked my interest.

Before downloading the app, I only had a vague understanding of the overall concept of how it worked but I figured, like with most apps, there would a tutorial on how to use it. So, hopeful and optimistic I downloaded the app to use on my iPhone and signed up for a year subscription with a 7 day free trial that carried the option to canceled anytime within the 7 day free trial without being charged.

Today is day 6 of my trial and sadly I don’t feel like I know much more about how to use the app than I did the day I downloaded it. There wasn’t any kind of tutorial on how to set-up or begin using the app. The first time I opened the app after downloading it asked me to log in then asked me to turn on notifications. Since I figured I would be about to turn notifications on later I opted not to turn any notifications on until I had a chance to check it out and set it up. After clearing the notification prompt it took me the “Right now” page, which was obviously blank because nothing had been created or scheduled yet, but that was it, there was nothing to direct me on where to go or what to do next. I was just left to figure out this app on my own which, for someone with ADD, isn’t exactly easy and the app isn’t particularly user friendly either.

However, because I had heard so many good things about this app I still wanted try it out. So I click on “Me” at the bottom of the screen which took me to what appeared to be settings and some information with links to blogs on different Neurodivergent subjects and management strategies, none of which were helpful in setting up this app.

Next I clicked on the Help Center link which took me to a website with Tech Support options for the Android, Apple IOS, Browser Versions of the app, and  one option for General support and inquiries. The General support link took me to a page that seemed like it might have some answers. There were four categories on the General page: What is Tiimo?, Technical, Subscription & Billing, and Contact Us. Under “What is Tiimo?” the first link was “How do I get started!”, finally, answers…or so I thought.

The information provided on “How do I get started!” was less of a step-by-step guide to setting-up and using the app and more of, or rather, actually a list of their “top 5 tips”. Which of the these 5 tips only 1 maybe 2 of them had anything to do with set things up in the app. The 5 tips listed in order are:

1) Set your schedule - Which is 4 sentences about how it takes time to fully integrate Tiimo and recommendations when to plan out your weekly schedule.

2) Create an activity, Create smaller steps with checklists, and Create a routine - Which instructs you on how to create an activity but they only provide screenshots on how to create a check list and a routine without actually explaining how to do it. 

3) Block out Free time - All they tell you here is not to over schedule yourself to make sure your day has planned breaks and blocs of free time but they don’t tell you A) if this is something you “Create” like the activities and routines or B) if it is, then how to create it.

4) Have fun! - They talk about how you can personalize Tiimo with icons, colors, and uploaded photos but again nothing how to do so.

5) Look back on the past week - Which is about discussing when Tiimo was helpful and and when it wasn’t over the previous week. Then using that information to continue setting up and fine tuning the app.

Not helpful.

So I went back to the General page and found a link for “Using Tiimo” I clicked it and it took me to another page that just says “Check out this really cool guide for you here!” The word “here!” is in bold to indicate another link. When I click on “here!” and it took me to yet another website claiming to help you get started with the app but the links that were listed started out with 1) Decide which devices to use, 2) Download the app, suscribe and sign up, 3) Get started which just took me right back to the 5 tips I previously mentioned.

At this point I had been battling my ADD for 6 days struggling to keep myself interested and focused long enough to figure out this darn app but after 6 days of feeling like I’d been running in circles, I was done. I don’t think I have ever had this much trouble, or any trouble for that matter, figuring out and using an app or a program, but for 6 days I tinkered, muddled, played, and messed with this app. I searched for any helpful information online and on social media all just to figure out and actually use this app.

No app should be this difficult nor take this much time to figure out, especially not one that is supposed to be designed and marketed specifically to help neurodivergent people; but if it’s not possible to make it less difficult to figure out and use, then you should at least have a Neurodivergent-friendly tutorial on how to set-up, integrate, and use the app. Although, several shorter tutorials might be better than one long tutorial for users who may struggle with focusing, holding interest, or remembering a lot of new information thrown at them all at once. These tutorials should be easily accessible, available to repeat anytime, and personally I prefer interactive tutorials. Physically going through a the actions of a new process helps me understand and remember it vs. listening to or reading about it.

I am truly glad this app has helped so many people. I was really hopeful that it could help me too but unfortunately it just left me frustrated, exhausted, and disappointed.

author: simsdvmphph

title: Very Happy ADHD Apple Watch User!
body:
I am really impressed with this app! I was expecting it to be a disappointment, as frankly most apps are, but this one has been a delightful surprise. I LOVE that not only does it have powerful capabilities on the Apple Watch (as opposed to claiming it works on the AW, but only providing one basic function as is typical for third party AW apps), but that it has a COMPLICATION for the AW! I am so appreciative of this!!! It boggles my mind how many developers put out AW compatible apps without bothering to go the extra step and create the corresponding complication! So thank you for that!!! 

I do have a few suggestions (I know, like everyone else). First, ADD folks tend to be very visual and color coding is often a big part of a useful organization system. The icons and color options for the dots are great, but I would like the ability to color code the whole routine or activity box as well. Also, having routines or activities that run simultaneously/overlap show up side-by-side on the screen. Finally, the ability to drag/drop unscheduled routines or activities to spots between scheduled things on any given day.

title: Without the bugs, this is 100% a 5 star app!
body:
I never write app reviews, but this app has made my ADHD so much more manageable! The visual aspects and using routines have been so helpful. I also love that I can use the notes section to make a running to do list that can quickly be popped into my daily schedule. 

Tiimo does better than what the iOS calendar, reminders, and notes apps did for me all together. I will definitely keep using it but a few of the bugs that have been really annoying are:

1. It’s nearly impossible to check off checklists on my Apple Watch, it just glitches out and won’t check off. It would be AWESOME to just use my watch for my “right now” tasks during the day, but I won’t even bother with it now.

2. When my “right now” task finishes, it doesn’t always go to the next task in my routine without me backing out of that tab and then going back to it.

3. Checking off a checklist and not ending the activity will often uncheck all the bullet points.

4. The worst one; widgets often won’t work. A sort of blank template placeholder will show up instead.

Despite the bugs, I seriously appreciate this app. I really hope they get fixed soon though because they’re really frustrating at times.

title: Time blindness

I have time blindness,I’ve noticed when scheduling on this app that I will cram too many things together, double book, or the opposite I’ll leave giant chunks of time open, that I did not notice was open, when I actually need to be doing something. Also being able to see my whole week at a glance in the app, like on the web browser, would be helpful. especially since the routines that you create in the app don’t show up on the web browser.

title: I keep coming back to it
body:
This app has been a lifesaver for my ADHD. It checks all the boxes- easy to schedule tasks, syncs with Apple Watch for easy tracking of next tasks, seamlessly keeps me moving throughout my day, ready-made routines, can be accessed via desktop anywhere (!!!!!!), and most importantly: easy to REORDER things and they magically get rescheduled correctly (omg this is probably the main reason I come back to Tiimo vs others). They keep updating the app and I just re-subscribed after finding out my old sub ended and other apps just didn’t do it for me. They either took too long to add a task (a deadly thing for ADHD brain) or restructuring the day was just AWFUL. Back to Tiimo it was.
One suggestion I have for making the latter even more seamless would be to have time slots visible during the  blank day to make scheduling tasks even easier (instead of having to select a time when creating or editing a task, just dragging it into the correct time slot or clicking/dragging he time slot to create a task would make it even easier for people like us with executive dysfunction.
Please, please do not stop supporting this app. <3

author: jenmar713

title: Would absolutely love but one GLARING error
body:
So this app is (almost) everything I’ve been looking for, so I truly hope this bug is updated soon, because to me this app could be as invaluable to me as Notion (and I live by Notion).

Time zones…pesky pesky time zones.
It doesn’t seem to recognize your phone’s time zone, or allow for users across multiple time zones.

For example, I have a work phone set in PST, but I live in CST so my personal phone is set in CST. With google calendar, if I set an event on my CST phone, it will make the correct conversion to PST when the google cal app is opened on my work phone. 

However, if trying to set up tasks in Tiimo on my CST phone, when I open the app on my PST phone, the task still shows in CST. That means I can mark “start” on a task in my work phone and accidentally skip hours of tasks on my CST phone. 

Just wish it was more multi-time zone friendly but alas, maybe I need to stick with google calendar

I’m going to be writing a blogabout my experience trying it for a week! I’m on day 5 currently! 

There are some great things about it! I love that it was created by women! I love the icons and start and pause! And they even have an option to share things you’d like to see in the app! It’s taught me a lot about myself , including needing to take deep breaths every time I’m timed out ! I love that you see that one activity has several task/checklist! I also need to check out those pre-created routines and activities! 

Even with the great things, I’m going to give it a week or two more and then I’m heading over to Routinery to try that program out!

author: itsapalindrome

title: Unique and worth it
body:
I’m an oddball and have tried every type of todo and productivity system under the Sun. I recently checked out Tiimo and have been loving it so far. 

The focus on structure, repetition, and focused time is so critical to how a lot of us work best - if you’re trying to do a James Clear Atomic Habits practice, there are few apps around the App Store this dedicated to that vision. 

Another huge difference for me is the dedication to breaking through the design ceilings in productivity app land - at the end of the day, 80% of every single todo app looks like a checklist with maybe a calendar and notes - they all look and feel the same after a while! Tiimo imagines a different way to work and visualizes it in a beautiful and innovative way. 

Same with the support and roadmap for Apple Watch - again for a neurodivergent like me, Apple Watch robust features are non negotiable for me - too many distractions on phone and tablet! 

Now the “bad news” is that this product is in BETA. There are bugs, syncing is a tad more bumpy than a fully established app would be, and there are some odd UI kinks and tiny feature gaps that might frustrate some users who come here from something like a Todoist. 

But it’s fully worth using for me today - maybe with hanging on to a couple apps for other parts of my workflow until Tiimo’s next few releases are under the belt. 

5/5 for the execution so far, the community feedback on their roadmap board, and most of all for their vision! It’s clear they truly “get” the challenges a lot of us face that traditional todo apps don’t help with. 

This is one to support and hope they grow and crush it!
author: Podcast EnjoyerR

title: Problems & Suggestions
body: Here’s some problems I came across. (1) I have vision problems and the times in My Day are a strain to see. I suggest enlarging the font. (2) The widget will say “Right now” for a task that isn’t happening now or soon. It’ll say that for a task an hour away. To avoid confusion, I suggest it say”Upcoming” for tasks that aren’t due yet and “Right now” when it is due. (3) When I complete a task early, I’ll still get a reminder to do that task and it’ll still appear on the widget. It doesn’t matter if I complete the circle and get confetti or if I go to My Day and delete it. It still shows. (4) I don’t always get reminded to do tasks even though I selected that option. A few times, I’ve checked my phone only to see a task halfway done. Very frustrating. (5) I love that I get to choose my own icons, but I suggest the window they first appear in be a circle rather than rectangle., so I can size it correctly. A few times, the final circle has cut off my image and I’ve had to resize it and the app saves both images. Being able to delete an image you no longer want would be helpful, too. (6) Sometimes I’ll add an item to a checklist I want to delete but there seems to be no way to delete it. The only option is to overwrite it but there’s nothing to overwrite. I want to delete. I’d also like to be able to slip in a task in the middle without having to overwrite the entire list. I’m deleting this app for now because the reminders are too unreliable, but if that gets fixed, I’ll come back. I’m a visual learner and I like the visual aspect of this.
author: Gm1234gm

title: Yes! Life/ADHD Friendly!
body:
This app is great!  I was recently diagnosed with ADHD as an adult and I’ve been trying to find tools that fit me…instead of putting stone of energy into doing things a neurotypical way and then either not succeeding or being excessively tired.

I’m not great at building habits or following through.  But this app is helpful in a lot of ways…

1) It helps me break things down.  It can be super overwhelming to get started…or easy to forget something that makes a task that much harder to do.  As I’m starting a task, I can look at the breakdown to get setup/mentally prepped.  And if I forget what I’m doing partway through - I can check again!!

2) It makes me think about time. Im always late, overcommitting, or unable to get to things because I run out of time.  As I’m setting things up in the app (which is actually a fun task for me) I am forced to think about time.  And when I see my day laid out with what I want to do, I’m often surprised about how much time I’ll need to actually accomplish things.  Seeing it like that helps keep me motivated to stay on track - or I’ll run out of time!

3) Yes to the colors and icons!!!  Im suuuuper visual - and I definitely get a dopamine hit from things that are color coded.  I keep a single color for a task so it is easier to identify what is grouped together.  And I just have fun picking icons for tasks or adding pics of my dog for all of pup care tasks - and of course it makes me happy to look at his face in the app haha.

Has this app fixed the challenges I have because if ADHD- absolutely not, and nothing will!  That’s not a reasonable expectation for any app.  But it helps me keep more energy for myself and keep in a more peaceful mindset - instead of needing to use it to remember things over and over again, feeling as stressed when planning/starting tasks, or being frustrated that I forget/missed something.

That said, here are a couple of things to note:
-There are some activities created for you, but to get the most out of it, you’ll need to take the time (and find the motivation) to setup customized tasks.  I think the colors/pics makes that more fun.
-The app is a bit glitchy every now and then. It might not save or has a delay in updating something that I’ve just saved.  Which seems to make the app spasm a bit and I will close and restart it.  It’s not excessive, but no one likes the feeling of “losing their work”.  Hoping these bugs will be fixed to make use more smooth!

All in all, I’m really appreciating this app and think it’s worth it!

author: Ayers5599

title: Almost perfect
body:
I love the idea of this app - everything down from being able to select emojis associated with each task and color code them is BRILLIANT. There was clearly input from the neurodivergent community and for that, I’m so appreciative! I love the notes feature as well - it’s so easy to get all my thoughts outs and then add them as tasks to my schedule later. 

However, the inability to use this app in its full glory across devices is a major downfall. For example, the routines that I create on the mobile app don’t sync onto the desktop version. Since I don’t always have my phone beside me, I often miss when routines begin, when pomodoro goes to break, or when I have an activity scheduled. 

There are also some glitches - for instance when I “pause” an activity it doesn’t actually seem to pause. When I press “start” again it just jumps to wherever it would have been if I’d never paused at all. 

For now I’m switching to another app, that isn’t as cool or as customizable or as detailed as Tiimo, but that is more cohesive across devices. If Tiimo develops a better desktop app that’s just as thorough and syncs up to the mobile app smoothly, I’ll certainly be downloading again. For me, unless I can have it on my personal computer, work computer, iPad, and phone, it just won’t be as effective.
author: smememeyes

title: Can be very helpful, but very buggy and learning curve is not great
body:
I’ve really enjoyed this app and it has helped me out a lot. However, the rigidity of it is very unhelpful for people with ADHD. 

I don’t know if this is a feature and my app is buggy, or if you simply can’t uncheck activities. Sometimes I’ll accidentally check an activity off in a routine and I can’t uncheck it! I’ll have to start the whole routine over to get back. 
This also affects when I go in and add something to a routine already in progress, since tiimo will suddenly skip me like 3 activities. I was barely on my 3rd activity, added one to my routine, and it skipped me to like the 6th. And of course, I couldn’t uncheck the checked activities, so I had to go and delete the routine, add it back, and start it over. 
I also wish we could add more time to an activity already happening. My time blindness makes it hard to figure out how long something will take me, and when I realize something will take me longer than I thought, I have to pause the activity and use an external timer, which mixes me up! Being able to restart an activity already in progress would be good too (sometimes I get distracted and can’t start exactly when it wants, but seeing it already started discourages me from getting back on track. 

I also think that the learning curve is very large, the initial app instructions are vague, and the blog posts linked are too many and too long with not enough screenshots just to get a barebones understanding how the app works. I’ve had more help watching youtubers use it than from the tutorials they have. 

I totally understand this is a work in progress, and I will continue to support the team of course. This has helped me get on track and balance my life much better. But the inflexibility is really frustrating and discouraging.

It’s super frustrating because I need an app like this to keep my life in order. I have horrible memory issues lately and this was my saving grace. I put several hours into setting up my routines and activities so it would be optimized for my use, and in the past week I have used it the issue has persisted every single day. 
I would love if this could be fixed. It is a paid service after all.

title: Sanity saver!!!
body: I don’t have an official diagnosis yet, but I have many symptoms of ADHD and just now discovering it in my 30s. I feel like so much of my life has been explained and time management has always been a struggle for me. I work full time, mostly remote, homeschool 2 of our 4 kids so far, and run a small business. I’ve been looking for something like this app for a long time. Paper planners only help for a short period of time for me and then I forget to check it and waste half of it. I love that this fills so many gaps I didn’t know I had or needed - the heads up notifications that a specific routine or activity is about to end or halfway done is awesome. So is the notes area where you can braindump a to do list or anything you want and then actually schedule it straight from there if needed at a later time. The integration with Apple Watch is also awesome bc I can put my phone away and have super focused time but still get the reminders I need (i know you can do focused mode on iPhone, but I’m still tempted to get distracted with my phone nearby). I’ve only had this app for a couple days and am still learning it but will definitely be keeping it past the trial! I love love LOVE this! Thank you so much for putting so much thought and intentionality into Tiimo!
author: TMLwood

title: A lot of potential, needs work
body:
Apple Watch app is basically not functional - can’t check off items, can’t go to the end of an activity (or skip). Doesn’t change between activities when the time runs out. This is a dealbreaker for me personally; I can’t be running to my phone between items in the routine. 

There seems to be some training required to use this app. For example, what on earth is the difference between an activity and a routine? Why can’t I have checklists in a routine? Why can’t activities be a part of a routine?

Excellent idea in this app: the “notes” section and the ability to drop tasks from there into your day. But the keyboard covers the part where you type, so it’s really hard to input tasks. 

I don’t love that the daily calendar UI shows my completed tasks/routines/activities. It creates a lot of confusion when looking at that screen. Would be helpful to have an option to turn this off or at least collapse the items in that section.  It’s also not clear why routines happen at “any time” by default - that seems to defeat the purpose of the calendar view. 

I would love to come back to this app when it can be used from the Apple Watch. I currently use Routinery but was looking for something that is a little more calendar-like so I can schedule around my work calendar. Unfortunately this is just not usable right now.

author: swamplillys

title: Big flaw hinders usefulness
body:
On the plus side this ap is attractive and fairly simple to set up with a little tinkering. I was in love with the idea of creating a block schedule that included a alarms, a visible timer, and checklists. Unfortunately I have found that the ap does not send me notification of scheduled events or tasks and the widget shows I have nothing planned for the day even when I do unless I reset the ap each morning (delete it and load it back onto my phone) and open it up again. That is really unacceptable to me. If an ap is unreliable sending notifications or I have to do something first to get it to send reminders than it is not functioning to help me manage my time. I am missing scheduled events or having to remember everything myself anyway. I guess this probably works fine for people who want to use to schedule time blocks on the fly but if you want to use it to prompt you to keep your schedule it fails. Really disappointing considered this is an ap you pay for.
Edit: after emailing with Tiimo, I was told the inability to send me notifications has to do with a limit set by Apple. While I sympathize that their hands might be tied by some restrictions in the IOS, it is hard to see how their solution - sending no notifications until I have already opened the app that day - is effective. Certainly other apps send me notifications before I have opened them that day - the notifications are WHY I opened those apps. Tiimo seems to have it the wrong way around by insisting you open the app before getting any notifications. 
Ultimately the explanation does not make Tiimo more useful to me, but I appreciate that they attempted to explain their viewpoint.

author: Asia Faoro

title: Visual timer is pointless if screen goes dark
body:
This app has good ideas, but it isn’t providing for the main reason I got it, which is to help with my daily routines.
1. There is no way to keep the screen from going dark during the timers, making the nice, helpful countdown visual pointless.
2. If the screen is on, the app gives a nice visual celebration when switching activities, but no noise whatsoever. If the screen is dark, I get a phone notification noise between activities. While doing activities, VISUALS and obvious SOUNDS are essential to know how much time I have left and when to switch to the next thing… especially if distracted or hyperfocused!!!
3. I like that you can schedule routines and they start automatically; however, it just starts in the background with no notifications and I need to remember to open the app to see the timers… which disappear in 1 min when my screen goes dark. And I have turned on every notification option available on the app.

I’m really struggling to understand how this app is helpful for ADHD without these things (unless you have a smart watch, in which case that should be clarified on the info page). It’s disappointing that I paid for a year subscription and now have to go back to setting individual alarms on my phone for these things while searching for a new app.

title: Almost My Favorite!

author: Smollfri

title: Be aware.
body: This app is pretty cool and works like it’s supposed too, but it is a subscription only app. You can’t access or use any of the features without paying a monthly or yearly fee for it. I dunno why they don’t just make it a paid app.
author: friiiiick

title: Good with the exception of one thing
body:
I love how this app allows you to add tasks to things that you need to get done (so like with breakfast or wind down for bed, it allows you to add each step that needs to get done before accomplishing those things to help make those activities less stressful). I haven’t been able to fully mess around with it to figure out how it fully works but the biggest thing I use it for is to remind myself to breathe throughout the day. I absolutely LOVE that throughout the timer set to do this, it does a countdown until it’s done and even has a celebratory screen halfway through! 
My one thing I found frustrating so far is that every now and then, it’ll sign me out so I don’t receive notifications and wind up not noticing for maybe a day or maybe longer since I often loose track of my days.
author: Forevermuic

title: Comprehensive and fun!
body: I never write reviews but I felt the need to tell people that this app has changed my life. I am a generally disorganized person but this app lays everything out on the table. I went in thinking “I’m not going to know how to do any fancy and specific things to fit my needs as a neuro-divergent person.” But anything I clicked I was able to edit, change, and personalize. It has been a life saver especially the reminders and notifications.
author: morticia's lover

title: (Updated) Only had for two days and it’s amazing
body:
I got this because I was having a really hard time managing my schedule and was falling very behind in my classes. This app is exactly what I’d been looking for and I love it so much! I’m going to be asking my family for a year subscription for Christmas! Update 4/13/21: I’ve had this for a while now and all I can say is that it just keeps getting better! Tiimo’s customer service is so nice and they actually consider what their users want in their app. The latest update is amazing with the ability to have freestanding activities and pause activities, and the way the time setup has changed is so much easier to use! I would recommend Tiimo to anyone who needs a little more consistency in their life. Their price after the free trial is reasonable and you get so much more than you pay for. Thank you Tiimo for being so wonderful!
Update 11/16/21: I’ve had this for about a year now and it’s still super great! They just updated again and it’s even better, I can’t remember what was added but I liked it 😆. Even though it has its occasional bug like any app, Tiimo is just such a life saver. As a senior in high school this year my schedule is crazyyyy. It’s very nice to be able to see my next event in the widget. With any luck I will get a smart watch for Christmas so that I can stay on track even better as I prepare for the transition to College! Shout out to the Tiimo Team for being such lovely people! 50/10 would definitely recommend
author: Hose Water

title: I really want to love this app.
body:
Pluses:
- The Apple Watch complication/app is the best feature. Being able to see my entire schedule and progress and checking things off on my lists without looking at my phone is fantastic. 

Deltas:
- The inability to reorder checklist items while editing routines seems like such a basic feature omission that it’s downright frustrating. Instead I have to create whole new items and delete old ones if I want to make any minor change in list order.
- The fact that “Share your day, tag us” is displayed under My Day and Right Now makes me feel as if the creators are more interested in marketing than developing an app with its users’ best interests in mind. Why would I want to share my day and open another distracting social media app when I’m already struggling to keep my day in order? 
- I wish I had the ability to turn off emoji and color customization for every single item. It feels more like a distraction and extra cognitive load than a useful tool for me.
- The Watch app keeps timing out and needs to log in every so often. Annoying and takes a couple of seconds.
- Updates to routines makes the app hang a few seconds with no indication in the UI.

I could say more but overall the app is just clunky with a convoluted finicky interface and an overemphasis on cute customization. I would really like to see a more streamlined and focused UI and/or better user onboarding/tutorials (without having to read through an overly long blog post). 

I’ll update my review as I continue to try and incorporate it into my daily ADHD routine for the next few days.
author: spiffyXD

title: Great app!
body: I just found this and I already love it. Accidentally logged in “edit mode” and was helped very quickly. Problem solved 🥰
author: Micunowska

title: Love this app, but …
body: This app is absolutely amazing. I loved having all the features on my watch to help keep me on task with things. I have adhd and asd and I loved using this, but unfortunately the app on both my iPhone and watch kept logging me out as soon as my wireless connection disrupted. This was so incredibly frustrating. No hints given here, but my email and passwords are too complicated and long to be forced to enter them continuously. Once this issue is fixed however, I will definitely be back to give 5 stars and subscribe.

body:
This needs a desktop app.
Access across multiple devices.
Activities and routines are good, but it’s too much detailed sometimes when not needed. But it’s a good one overall.
author: Prasadrak

title: Great if it works
body:
Logs me out on my Apple Watch (I’ve had to log back in anywhere from daily to several times a day  Takes days to erase deleted activities/routines, Doesn’t always send notifications, Doesn’t sync well between iPad, iPhone and Apple Watch I’ve seen people claim you can use a website version on a pc and you really can’t. There’s virtually no features/functionality on the website. Also don’t bother syncing your calendar with it, it will default to the calendar so if you have any all day events in your calendar or have a routine or activity you do during an event, those activities either won’t start or won’t send you notifications. 

When it works it’s amazing. But this is the glitchiest, buggiest app I’ve EVER used

Unfortunately this makes it useless for me :/
author: Happiness seeker 123

title: Amazing app, needs some work
body: I LOVE how this app is laid out, and how it reminds me of my daily routines and appointments (especially on the Apple Watch), but it is a little buggy. Items will randomly disappear from my calendar view, I will schedule something as recurring and it won’t “take” (I have to try a few times) and it’s ALWAYS logging me out on my watch. It’s bearable enough to keep using it but I hope they work those things out because it’s otherwise perfect and really helped me stay on task.
author: HollyKhayos

title: Improving, but there are still problems
body:
I fully acknowledge that this app is a work in progress, and is getting a little better with every update. But there’s still a perpetual problem where as soon as Tiimo is updated, a new feature is rolled out, bugs are fixed and glitches are patched, there is always another problem or new bugs that come up when it seems to be improving. It’s like one step forward and two steps back. I don’t quite understand that because the concept and design of this app seems pretty simple (although I’m sure there’s more to it under the surface). 

I don’t know, I’m just trying to get through my days, get stuff done and not let ADHD (and what I suspect is ASD) get the best of me. This app helps some, but the benefits kind of become redundant when I have to manually go in and correct things because little bugs in the program throw off my routine. The one I’m the most frustrated with right now is the fact that Tiimo likes to log me out of the app on my Apple Watch randomly - it almost always happens overnight, and it sometimes when I’m in the middle of an active routine, and I don’t realize until more time than I had intended to spend on an activity has passed and then “whoops! I have to enter my log-in information again.” 

If you have ADHD or are on the autism spectrum, you know how frustrating and discouraging interruptions to routine can be, especially in their early stages before you’re fully comfortable with them.
author: CalvinationStation

title: Every update, same problem
body: Every time this app gets updated, I get kicked out. And then I can’t log back in. And then I asked for my password to be requested and I never get the email. Then I have to contact customer service, and they have to manually reset my password but only after going through all the stupid steps that don’t work first. And then it last for three months, and then I get kicked out and have to start all over again. It’s not worth it. I’m so over this.

body: I love how customizable this app is without being cluttered or hard to understand. author: Catapus

title: The best
body:
as an autistic person with chronic illness, i need reminders to properly take care of myself and function in the best way i can. i’ve tried an incredible amount of apps & methods to make this work but tiimo is by far the most accessible, including the price, which is about what i would spend on a good planner for the year. the app layout is very clean and not overwhelming which i find essential. i love the way you can add emojis & colors for the task icons, though i wish there was a way to customize the theme color. i also find it extremely helpful that you can connect to your calendar app.  i use this feature for my work schedule & appointments. 

i would fully recommend tiimo to anyone who needs a visual idea of their day and/or anyone who relies on reminders to get through each day. this is a great app to support and utilize with great people behind it listening & improving

title: Great app, hoping for small changes
body:
I don’t have adhd or autism but this app has helped me to reflect and improve on my routines and systems a lot. It’s one of the best calendar / routine apps since Google Calendar , which is saying a lot bc GCal was the standard for years and over these past few months I’ve already fallen in love with tiimos capabilities. Only thing is I am unable to use the new Widget functionality on the app which I was looking forward to. I have the latest tiimo version so I’m not sure why it’s not available for my iPhone? What would really make this app spectacular is if it had 2-way sync with Apple Calendar /Google Calendar and if there was a way to block other apps while using this app.

Nevertheless I’m excited for what’s to come feature wise with this app as its grown so much, if these features could also be taken into consideration I’d appreciate
author: habits are a blessing

title: Life Automation
body:
I’m actually really impressed with this application, but at almost 30 a year it’s pricey for an application. Not saying it’s not worth it but I hold it to much higher standards then a free application. 

User Interface / Aesthetic ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
First of all the UI is great. It’s simple, and very personable. You pick your main color as long as light or dark mode. The fonts are sleek and modern. The icons are personable. The user interface takes a little bit to get used to but the whole app follows the same interface motion principles so it’s easy to catch on. 5/5 for the UI.

Organization⭐️⭐️
The organization is okay but there should be much more. I would love to be able to indent checklist items to be under another item. Or even put activities under other activities. 

I got this app in order to automate my life with that I wanted to create a morning routine. In my morning routine I have three activities that have many tasks and are very different. Although yes you could sort with colors I cannot separate the timing, or completion aspects.

I also don’t like or understand the separation of activities and routines. Both are important and need to be done. But when you separate them it becomes confusing.

Also when you have multiple activities some being at a certain time some not it becomes VERY clunky. There’s not a way to my knowledge to condense them down, most of the time you can only see 4 activities at a time making it easy to forget activities at the bottom. When you check off an activity it still stays at the top cluttering up the screen. 

During Activity⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Overall great allows you to separate and see a filling circle as the timer, allows you to check off the tasks and isolate your focus. 

Maybe add an alarm to go off after the activity is complete? There is a notification but it’s not noticeable if actually doing a task. Or even take it a step further and integrate a Spotify API to play your playlist until the activity is done. 

Other addition ideas to make this app better: 
- I noticed there’s no siri or shortcut integration. It would be really cool to be able to program nfc to work with the app 

- add urgency level 

- be able to create a key for the colors and what they represent 

- be able to complete a task throughout multiple days, for example if you have a big project with 10 steps and want to work on it for 30 minutes a day 

I will say that I am still learning the app, and will continue to update this review as I know more (:
author: ashleyjdksoosodjmxlls

title: Huge potential. But quite glitchy.
body:
The layout visually is a dream; all is tidy for glancing at. The potential here is actually huge for what the app sets out to do. Unfortunately it's basically still in a buggy beta mode. Even so, I want to stick around to see if they'll fix the bugs and optimize the vision, because if they do, it could be one of the very best of its category. The blogs are really great, laid out nicely and are informative / interesting. But hopefully the layout will become more intuitive for each section and function so that it won't require a deep dive on how-to this or that.

Issues / Requests:

• Can't reset an activity once it's begun.

• If you adjust the activity order by sliding them into different positions, they will force-reset to the original order if you change apps or close and re-open the app. Other times when the order looks correct, pressing an activity will cause it to glitch back into the original order, revealing you've activated a different activity than it displayed at first.

• Sometimes it won't let you check off an activity.

• I would like to customize a sound for each activity as I read was possible, but I don't see that option through any settings or editing. 

• Would be nice to just tap the activity from the list to view it full screen instead of going to the Right Now section. 

• Accessing the Library through the Library icon (beside the + sign for adding an activity ... kind of unclear unless you accidentally find it) to switch to Routines and/or attempt to create a Routine will result in blanked out options, the inability to return to the Activities list, and / or ultimately a dead end, meaning you'll need to force-quit the app and open it again.

• Would be nice to have a setting for automatically starting an activity from a designated finished activity, so that if you want to tie several together seamlessly you could without breaking focus. I think this might be part of the Routine section under development. 

• Not sure what the Notes section is about. 

Hopefully I don't come across as being too merciless with my critique here, hah! But I do look forward to seeing this app accomplish its potential.
author: crumb collector

title: Helpful and a little buggy
body:
This app has helped me so far. I like that I can make a checklist of items to complete within one task which helps remind me even further about what I need to do. I’ve noticed a couple things that bug me though (sorry if these are a repeat of other reviews):
1. The reminder notification that comes through 9 minutes before a scheduled task says 9 “seconds” which alarms me at first and then irritates me because it’s wrong

3. Would like to add tasks as repeating at 2 or 3 times per week, but can only repeat tasks at finite intervals

Otherwise I’m happy that I have this app and look forward to seeing improvements. The visual and simple interface is comforting to my overstressed brain :)

author: NoahKale

title: Missed the mark for me
body:
Everybody has already mentioned the good, and I agree with much of it.

The bad: 
- Not at all useful for moderate to heavy time blindness. I set an interval timer to go off every six minutes which sorta keeps me on track… lots of people with time blindness just need that level of nudging. Even being able to set halfway, quarter way, eighth way or whatever notifications would help. One notification when a task is transitioning without any prods about how much time has gone by or whether or not I actually switched tasks will only keep me apprised about what I’ve failed to pay attention to for the past hour. You really need multiple notifications for anything other than extremely light time blindness. If I remembered to look at my device every so often to stay on track then I would need this app.

-Syncing is unreliable. Frankly, this instantly makes the app a non-starter for any professional.

-The scheduling is too rigid. For example, sometimes I don’t know in advance if I’m going to make coffee at home or hit the coffee shop. I should be able to have that still be a block in my morning routine without prescheduling it between taking my meds and checking my email. Editing things is a pain.

-Poor event collision notification

-The event adding/routine-making mechanics are clunky. Took me like an hour to even reason about the best way to structure the first 2 hours of my day using their UI idioms and then when I realize I need to change one thing, I need to manually change every thing before or after that was affected by the change. Given, I’ve been making interfaces for a long time, but I could immediately see several ways to improve the operation dramatically.

-The web interface is seriously hobbled because it’s free, so you have to use the app even though data entry in a device is way slower.

And I just keep thinking… this is supposed to be for people with ADHD? 😕 This app clearly has helped a lot of people, but some of it is downright painful for many members of a target audience.
author: andythechef

title: I love this app!!
body: This app is so helpful for me. I have anxiety and depression which challenges me daily to keep a schedule, but Tiimo is very helpful and honestly I look forward to using it every day. I am excited to go back to school after summer so I can fully experience Tiimo’s help.
author: psq1230

title: A great concept that needs work
body:
Tiimo has a lot of potential, but falls a bit short in usability for now. Setting up your routine for the day is somewhat clunky, but no doubt improves with practice and customization. I’ve found the app somewhat buggy.

Things have disappeared from my schedule. Adding activities and lists is a bit difficult. The keyboard covers the part of the screen where you’re typing the next list item, and emojis/symbols don’t consistently load. Though I have notifications turned on, Tiimo has not notified me of anything. This makes it difficult to see how this is actually useful for time management. For example, I was using the pomodoro routine today, and nearly worked through a break I’d been waiting for. Tiimo wouldn’t allow me to adjust the break time, instead either pushing ahead or requiring me to pause the whole routine.

I feel like this app could be very useful, but with the existing bugs, I don’t find it worth the subscription price. I’ll keep checking in as it progresses. For now, my search for the ideal ADHD app continues.

author: Yung Nik

title: Lots of potential
body:
Having a visual scheduler with a timer attached has been helpful during my test run of the app these last few days. I will be paying for it when my free trial is up.
However, that’s partly for the potential I see in the app, and their good communication about the app development roadmap.
I am looking forward to the release that will improve routines.
A few things I would find very helpful:
-activities that are proportional to their size, so a 2 hour activity is four times as long as a half hour activity, etc. 
-Activity templates with more organization options, rather than a list of things I’ve made lately. And doing Delete This And All Future can’t delete the template.
-A button that takes me back to the current day and time, rather than scrolling back up or having to pick out the correct day of the week up top (that last is actually a little hard for my particular brain).

And thank you for working to build an app for neurodivergent brains!
