author: Kat246900

title: Great start, will stick around for more…
body:
I enjoy that this app gives me a visual schedule of my day.  There are some features that I really feel are missing: 
1. Drag and drop to adjust times of routines or activities. Calendar items would be locked/static and then tasks can shift around as needed between scheduled events. 
2. Visual representation of gaps in the day. I like how the Structured app does this. It shows how much time there is between tasks/events on your schedule and asks if you would like to add anything.  Also their time blocks(bubbles) are larger or smaller based on the length of the task/event. 
3.  Option to add routines to schedule based on end time rather than start time.  This takes away the headache of doing the mental math of trying to plug tasks/routines into my schedule. For example I want to leave the house or be in bed by a certain time and that changes from day to day. I would like to be able to set my morning / evening routines accordingly. Or have my afternoon chore routine complete by the time I start cooking dinner. 
I’m looking forward to seeing what’s next!

nothing you say is there is there. i have to come up with everything, theres no preset routines, theres no pictures. theres just a million options for data entry which the whole

author: George Donskoy

title: Love this app, but i would recommend some improvements
body:
I’m autistic and have ADHD and I love this app! Some improvements I would suggest are:

The ability to color code even more! I would love to be able to color-code the white background (not just the icon) of activities, especially based on categories like school or work. Like if all of my school items could have orange backgrounds and all of my home activities could be blue, but then those have individual icons or something that would be nice. It would really help my visual brain not get overwhelmed by my schedule and have a clearer picture of whether my day is balanced in my mind.

title: Time changes!
body: I set up an entire routine and when I apply that routine to a specific date, the time changes. Very frustrating
author: delizo2

title: This app disappointed me
body: I feel like if you’re going to have people sign up for a subscription just make a separate app for that and let it be the pro version since you are sort of scamming everyone when they first download this app since not everyone has a credit card and some people have strict parents so if you fully understand that and just make this the free version and make the other app where you pay this app will make a big difference and will probably be in the top free 200 apps in the category it’s for.
author: kenniejeon

title: Wife with Autism, Husband on Night Shift
body:
This app is a lifesaver. My husband’s work schedule shifts between 12 hour day and night shifts. I have a solid day routine but when he works nights, I fall apart. I don’t know when to sleep, eat, do household chores, make dinner, etc. Enter Tiimo. 

A neurodivergent creator on TikTok recommend this app so I gave it a try. I sat down and thought out a routine for when he works on night shift and also a routine for when he has a day off but still needs to stick to his night shift sleeping schedule. It’s been amazing so far. No more oversleeping on my part while getting nothing done and he’s been sleeping a full 8 hours. Meals have been on time and the house is clean! My night shift dread and anxiety has finally gone away. I’m actually thinking about buying an Apple Watch so I can have my routine on my wrist at all times. 

Thank you so much for developing this app. No other time blocking or scheduling software has worked for me in the past. I Bullet Journal, but again, it’s not quite as effective as seeing my routine in real time and being able to be reminded of what I’m supposed to be doing. 
This app will change lives.
author: thebrisknees

title: A step in the right direction
body: I was very excited to use this app given the companies interest in creating an app designed to help those with time management issues due to a divergent mindset. Reproducible routines are a step in the right direction however, the app, like most others, doesn’t address the problems of rigid scheduling and the resulting negative reinforcement which are both easily solved with paper. Hoping they get it.
author: Andrew Thomas Nelson

title: Subscription Based App
body: As a neurodivergent person I need help structuring my day and functioning productively, I was excited to find this app then realized it’s only by subscription. Its upsetting seeing an app that prides itself on offering accessibility to nd people but limited to only those that can afford it. I’d even put up with ads!
author: Auserie Boling

title: figure it out
body: what a disappointment. super glitchy. i created an account, set my theme, explored the nooks and crannies of the app and was very excited to use it. i immediately added a task, created the checklist, selected a cute icon and color, and pressed start. swiped over to the "right now" tab and was delighted with the visually appealing timer, with my tasks clearly laid out in front of me. i got to work right away. ten minutes later, i looked up to see a black screen. the app had suddenly closed, and logged me out. i tried fruitlessly to log back in, multiple times. i restarted the app. i restarted my phone. eventually i deleted the app and redownloaded it to see if it would help. each time i tried to log in, i received an html error code, or an error that said "user could not be authenticated" or something like that. what the heck. after digging through some reviews, i see that this is not an uncommon problem. this unfortunate error totally disrupted my workflow, and i am frustrated with this outcome. all i can say is i am so glad there was a free trial option so i didn't waste my money on this app. great concept, poor execution. i will check back in a few months once the developers have gotten help and worked out some of the serious bugs & kinks!
author: bblessdd

title: This app really helped me out
body: This app was incredibly helpful for me. It helped me with school so much, especially during the pandemic. Unfortunately I don’t need it anymore as I have graduated but I’d absolutely recommend it to any student neurodivergent or not and will certainly use it if I ever go back to being a student.
author: Dylan NgChow

title: So thankful
body: Thank you for making this app. I am autistic and have a degree of adhd to top it off. This app really helped me finally feel grounded. I have tried many schedule apps and have struggled. The visual cues are what truely makes this app shine for me. I would love to see more visual customizations in the future. Maybe pictures as well as icons? Again I am so great full for this app and all the it supports me with. I highly recommend it!!!
author: Lake Hylia

title: FANTASTIC app & have suggestions!
body:
This app is the best scheduler for me, especially since I can make a widget on my Home Screen to remind me of what I need to do whenever I pick up my phone. Combined with reminder notifications, this 100% prevents me from forgetting stuff! And I LOVE having the ability to designate certain tasks as things that can be done anytime during the day (I’ll call these Anytime Activities).

My only qualm is that Anytime Activites don’t show up in the Right Now view or in the Widget. So here’s a feature/tweak I would love to see: a button to show/hide Anytime Activities in the Right Now view, along with an option in Settings to set whether Anytime Activities are displayed in the Widget. That way, people who like how it functions right now can keep it like that.

Anyway, my favorite part about this app is that the Widget displays bright colors and pictures that I can’t overlook on my Home Screen. Tiimo is fantastic and I’m excited to see it continue to improve!

I also have ADHD and that makes it even harder to schedule everything. But I love the new update! I can actually schedule things without a time so I can put all my business tasks I need to get done there for the day. And I can still schedule my meals and appointments to the hour.

author: aWyldeHeart

title: Does NOT help w/ ADHD
body: It’s a lovely concept, but the app is NOT helpful for ADHD. People with ADHD struggle with time blindness, meaning they underestimate the amount of time it takes to do a task. So you end up not done with something you scheduled, and the app is already promoting you to begin the next task. Also, people with ADHD struggle to start tasks and stay on track, but the app only sends one reminder at start time and end time. Suggestion: for ADHD, the app should send multiple reminders to keep us on track. Also, there should be the option to extend the amount of time for a task and automatically move up the other task (except for fixed time tasks like meal times and appointments).
author: ashleyk11

body: I’ve tried out just about every planner app there is to offer and this is the only one that works for me. Can’t wait to see the great this the developers are going to do in the future with Tiimo!
author: cemu99

title: I love this! Two suggestions though
body: I’m autistic and I love this app! I get depressed when I don’t have an externally imposed routine and this helps create that for me and literally avoid depression! I love the interface and the colors. Two ideas: color themes - you can pick in the settings which color scheme you’d like and then when you select the color for an event it gives you those colors as options. For example I love neon colors or pastels and I wish it let me pick one of those as a theme so I didn’t have to build a bunch of custom colors. Second idea: make the ability to not give a task a duration. Sometimes it gives me anxiety to put a duration on something that I don’t know how long it’ll take. On these tasks we could simply check them off when we’re done. It would ease a lot of stress in creating schedules.
author: italian speaker

title: A Game-Changer
body:

I love how this app is easy to navigate with endless customization options, and I’ve recommended it to people of all ages. It doesn’t feel like I’m using an app made for a toddler, and even my neurotypical friends say that the format has helped them too.

Bonus points for being a small company run by neurodiverse individuals and for an engaging blog presence touching on a variety of important topics. Worth every single cent.

author: Jacob E Hartman

title: I really want to like this
body:
I really want to like this app, so much so that I paid for a year upfront without reading any reviews. My bad. I like the look of it, and I like the idea, but actually using it is way more complicated than it needs to be.

Problems I’ve run into in my first 24 hours:
-can’t click and drag checklist items
-an item I allotted 30 minutes for keeps resetting to 24hrs 30min
-can’t reorder activities on iPhone that are set to “any time”
-when viewing the calendar on desktop (chrome) that I created on iPhone, only one activity shows up for today and it’s one I’ve already completed. The other activities I have scheduled for today are not shown.
-when I add an activity to my day on desktop, it still does not show on desktop (I can only see the same one completed activity as before), but it does appear on iPhone.
-on desktop I cannot zoom out to view a whole week, I can only see 4 days at a time. I also cannot zoom in to see just today.
-on the other side of that coin, on iPhone I cannot zoom out to see more than one day at a time.
-if an activity is not assigned assigned a specific time, and it is checked off, I feel it should go to the bottom of the day. Instead it still takes up a bunch of space in the middle of the day even though I no longer need to think about it.
-on my “right now” view on iPhone, the description spot for one activity shows the description I put for a different activity. Both activities show the same description. When I return to “my day” the descriptions show correctly. Unpausing and re pausing the activity switches which description shows on both activities (most recently active shows on both).

The desktop calendar is totally unusable for me, and the iPhone app is... usable but barely. I hope to see these issues fixed, because if this system works properly, I would love to use it and don’t mind paying for it. But for now, I can’t recommend it.

Edited to add: less than three hours after submitting this review I now receive an error message logging in. After logging in, I am offered the various subscription plans, even though I already purchased an annual subscription. Logging out and logging back in, restoring purchase, nothing works. When I click restore, it says there is a problem retrieving the receipt. I can no longer access my account on iPhone, which is the only platform it was even half useful on for me. I have now cancelled my subscription within the free trial period.

If I hear that these functionality issues have been addressed, I would love to subscribe again and would be happy to pay for an app like this. Hopefully I will still be able to do a free trial next time, as I have seen enough for now to know this isn’t going to work without some serious updates, but would want to try out a future version before committing again.

author: KCKMom

title: so far amazing with a few suggestions
body:
my reasoning:
- when i save a routine and try to add it to another day it only adds a portion of the routine (like for my getting ready to leave i have things like get dressed, pack bag, and brush teeth but it only added get dressed when i tried to add the routine). it would also be great if you could make the routine feature have a way to add one activity at a time but still have all the activities stores under the same routine. allowing editing of the activities while it’s in the routine as well would fantastic as well. 
- there needs to be a way for the activity log to have two sorting options: name and time frame. i usually put in my classes and such at the beginning of each term yet sometimes things change and i need to add an additional class meeting for say finals or something but i can no longer find that activity i created at the beginning of the month. that means i have to recreate it and go back to find what color i labeled it with and such yet i have about 15 “shower” blocks in a row in the activity tab because i shifted the time frame of those most recently and that feels excessive and unproductive. there needs to be a way to save one of each activity i create under its name and disregard the timing/frequency it’s used. please add a subsection of the activity log that has one of each activity i’ve created sorted alphabetically by name and if you really want to make me happy add a search feature to that section as well.
- would really like a feature that allows me to schedule time to take my medicine during other activity without the app and website freaking out that i overlapped the times every time i open the planner. it’s so nice when i make planning mistakes but i don’t want to have two homework blocks surrounding the reminder to take my medicine especially since i can’t alter the notifications for each specific activity. so really this is two suggestions: 1. allow me to signal to the system that i know things are overlapping for certain activities and it’s okay and 2. let me alter the notifications for the start/end of each individual activity. the notification settings across the app determine default notifications but i can choose to change them for individual activities as well. 

i hope the future holds partnerships that help make this app free for the portions of the neurodivergent community who can’t afford the fee.
**this is an updated review after using the app for a month as of 3/9/2021
author: keriwozz

title: I have been waiting for this app for ages, but it’s green
body:
I have literally been waiting for an app like this (that allows for some sort of integration of my events, tasks, and general time keeping) for ages. I know there are apps out there that already do something like this, and some of them do portions of it somewhat well, but they generally are extremely clunky, convoluted and somehow manage a mix of too many and at the same time not enough customization (🤷‍♂️). 
And when I refer to the blend of those items it is often best if the app can just pull in from existing sources (easy for calendars, often not so easy for tasks). 

So when I saw Tiimo, what it could do, the fact that it *looked* pleasing/had a nice UI AND had an Apple Watch app?! Heck yes, definitely wanted to try it. As the app is only a few months old I’m not surprised there are some gaps, but based on what I’m seeing the developers are working hard to fill them!

I noticed that they are working on adding tasks with no fixed start/end time (currently you can only add a task to a specific date, with a specific start and end time. And from there your only quick option is to start the task) & they are adding a search feature to the task list (you can add common tasks that you perform to a template list & they have a fairly well populated pre-made template list as well!). 

I’m not sure how it would fit in with the changes being made, but as one who subscribes to the GTD method what I really would need to have to keep using the app is an ‘inbox’. Sometimes I just need to jot down my tasks so I don’t forget what they are, other times I have enough, well, time to fully detail/log the task and when I want to do it. 
I was thinking of just putting them in the templates list, but this would just get really really cluttered without a way to differentiate between the two (keeping in mind, the whole point of the inbox is to add quickly so adding a color or other flag to inbox items would sort of defeat the purpose). 
And with the ability to not have a fixed start/end time it would be nice to have some sort of ‘auto scheduler’ - whether it’s ‘I have x amount of free time & I am in Y location (and ideally with Z contexts as filters 😉), what can I get done? Or just a more basic one with the app noticing you have free time and suggesting to add items from your inbox to your schedule. 

Anyway - great app so far! Definitely going to keep an eye on it!
author: appoli13

title: I adore this app
body:
This app is amazing for me as someone with ADHD. The visual timer with the added notifications for beginning, halfway, and end of a task really ease any anxiety that comes from wondering how long I’ve been doing a thing. 

The only addition I would ask for is a sort of “nag” function. Maybe it asks if I want to start every x amount of minutes and won’t until I say yes? I have a bad habit of seeing the event start and if I’m not quite ready, it leaves my mind. But if I could maybe add 5min and it asks me again, or similar, it’s much easier for me to remember and get started on my task because it won’t allow me to forget.

Thank you so much for this app. Life is a little less chaotic with it
author: Ephodia

title: Lovely app except some glitches.
body:
Great visual time keeper great for my ADHD. 

For some reason, almost every button has been seemingly shortened. For example, when I go to add a task, Why is “add time” shortened to “ad...time” ? This is frustrating and makes it take more cognitive effort to figure out what’s going on. Must be a glitch, could be solved by allowing users to adjust the text size themselves which might also increase accessibility. 

Also, please add the ability to collapse calendar notes. The automatic Zoom calendar invite comes with soooo much info that when automatically displayed in tiimo, it takes so much time to get an overview of my day. 

Overall, great app. I think if you could improve “glance-ability” or the ease at which I can concisely understand what’s going on, this app would truly shine.
author: Booberrox392

title: A little glitchy
body:
Hi,

A disclaimer: I just downloaded the app yesterday so I may not know how to navigate it yet fully. I added Tiimo as a widget and I wanted to be able to see what I need to be doing at a glance without opening the app. However, it has had the same display message yesterday saying “This was it for today, see you tomorrow 👋” when I still had an activity to do. The widget had worked properly when the Tiimo sign up activity occurred, but not now. I thought maybe the problem was that the activity I had scheduled was between two days of the week (10 pm - 1 am). But I adjusted the time to 10 pm - 11 pm and the message didn’t show up either. I also turned notifications on (I had turned all of them off because the widget would work just fine for me) but that didn’t solve the problem either. I was able to get the notification on my iPhone’s home screen, but the widget still said the “This was it for today, see you tomorrow 👋”.  Also, when I checked the app to see what was going on, it said my activity was already over, which is not true since it just started when the notification popped up. Therefore I can’t see the visual timeline of how long I have until my activity is over, because it claims it already happened. I would like to use Tiimo for that purpose of letting you visually see how much time you have left, I think that would really help me out. But I can’t see it using the widget or when I open the app. I rated 5 stars because the app is really cool and it has a lot of potential. Also this is super super nit picky (I have OCD in addition to the reasons why I use this app 🙄), but if there was a way to delete “My icons” from the photo menu, that would be cool too because I selected something that I didn’t want for an activity one time and now I have to see it every time I go to set a picture for an activity. That is probably the last priority on your update list but I just thought I would mention it. Thank you so much for all your hard work!

The only thing I have a problem with is that as of right now, it doesn’t sync up to other calendars. I use my Apple calendar for “non normal” things like appointments that won’t be reoccurring. author: Anneliese~

title: Poor Tech
body:
Very disappointed. I, like many other reviewers, could not log in. First, it couldn’t find my account (depending on the method used to access their website). Then my password with letters couldn’t be used to log into the app (there’s only a numbers pad in app). After resetting the password to all numbers, it was back into the loop of not having a valid account...

I made several attempts to get support from Tiimo but they were not helpful and didn’t seem to understand/have a method for looking directly into my account or fees charged. Instead they gave vague general troubleshooting instructions and never resolved the issue. 

I’m a therapist who was excited to try this out before recommending it to clients. I will not be doing so. I’m fairly patient and tech savvy but I understand some of my clients would be frustrated beyond measure with this app & the support team. Thankfully other options are readily available...

title: Great idea, could benefit from more flexibility
body: This tool has a lot of great features. I just started using and am just learning my way around. However, I would appreciate if we could put time parameters around things within a certain category, rather than creating multiple entries. For example, I would prefer to have an entry that says “workout (6a-7a)” that within you could establish “stretch 6-6:10, cardio 6:10-6:40, cool down 6:40-7.” The only options I see are to either create new entries for each, or do one entry and use the checklist. However, you lose the time management piece with the checklist. For me, since I categorize these 3 actions as part of a workout, I’d rather not break them into different entries because it becomes too cluttered for my preference.

title: Mixed bag
body:
There are a lot of things I love about this app. The graphics the visual design the use of checklists to make sure I don't forget things. I love the reminders. 

Two things in particular really bother me though. The limited smart watch compatibility which means I'm being forced to choose between app compatibility and other key functions I want like stress monitoring which I could have with a fitbit. I don't like the notifications directly on my phone because it forces a distraction I don't need. Also I might leave my phone beside my bed to go brush my teeth and wash my face so the app doesn't work as well without a watch.

I'm also struggling to connect to the web calender. I work nights and can't get any customer service and the faq/help sections are a joke tbh. I'm super stressed trying to deal with it which is kind of counter productive. It also won't accept my password which I had saved and apparently fixing this issue isn't as easy as submitting a request either. I can't view any account information on the app either including what email I might have signed up with.

Overall I'm only giving it 3 because I really like the functionality of the app but the other issues have me reaching for my anxiety meds because I'm 90 minutes in and I've made 0 progress with little hope of help in the foreseeable future.

author: Cams🖤

title: Love this app!
body:
I absolutely love this app, it is pretty much exactly what I’m looking for.  I do have a few requests that I think would really help me and maybe others. 

1. The only thing I don’t like about this app is the way the notifications work.  As someone who hyper fixates on things the quick ding isn’t enough to get my attention and move on to the next task.  If there is some way where there could be an alarm sound (maybe as an option if others don’t want it) or to have the phone vibrate for a few seconds.  I just need it to last longer than the typical “ding” and I can’t find a way to do it in settings for just this app.  I’m not sure if there’s a way to fix this within development, but even a sound or vibration that goes off while in the app would be helpful.  I could just leave the app open while doing my work. 

2. I would also love the option to have more flexibility with the day.  Although I definitely understand that many people using an app like this are using it for structure, I would like the option to have scheduled tasks and unscheduled tasks.  This way I don’t have to make it so minute to minute.  So basically I would be able to have “study” and I could set it for an hour duration but not have to schedule it for a specific time.  When I feel like studying I could click “start studying” and it would set an hour timer or something.  I have ADHD and get distracted very easily so the whole minute to minute planning doesn’t always work since I end up falling behind.  I think having the option to not schedule every task for an exact time would be perfect for me.

title: I LOVE this app, but there are a couple kinks
body:
As someone who is neurodivergent, this app has helped me bring order and structure to what was an overwhelming amount of unstructured time. I highly recommend trying it for a couple weeks if you think you’ll benefit, because you’ll probably find it as helpful as I did.

Now for why I docked a star: there are a couple of things that could really improve the app. A search feature for the icons would streamline use. More background colors as well (especially a white background option) would be nice, as I’ve found I run out of color coding colors quickly. Also, being able to schedule multiple things at one time (such as eating lunch while at work) and being able to more easily repeat activities on the same day (rather than just the next day/ week at the same time) would be great for those of us who take meds more than once daily and while doing other things. Finally, adapting the app to be available to sync on the smarter FitBit devices would be VERY helpful (I’d gladly pay a fee to download it onto my device if that’s what it takes). Though these would make the app better and more useful, it’s already pretty great, so if I had the option to give it 4.5 instead of 4, I would have.

author: Elle🦁🐶🐝🐙(munchkiiwii)

title: Unintuitive, missing basic functionality, buggy
body:
If you look at the help guide on iPad in landscape mode, the top section of text isn’t visible, but there’s no indication that it’s cut off, so you just see a strangely unhelpful series of images without context — until you get to the final screen where the image overlaps the text and it looks like the app is just badly designed. 

When you tap the plus button, there are three options that appear. But for some reason only one option appears first and the other two are withheld for a second, so it’s easy when you’re starting out or are in a rush to tap the pill thinking it will open a submenu. In other words the interface can trick you into choosing the wrong function every time you tap the plus button.

If you try to create a routine but you haven’t created activities yet, you will get a blank-ish screen with instructions to create an activity, with an arrow that points to a blank space. Tapping the blank space does nothing—in other words, the plus button isn’t just invisible, it’s completely missing. There is no way to create a routine until you create activities first. 

You’re forced to assign starting times to everything you create. What if I want to create a daily routine with a variable start time? I don’t want to see an indicator that I’m “late” to start the routine, and I don’t want alerts telling me to start it before I’m ready. I just want to know that the daily routine is waiting for me to start it when I’m ready. This app won’t let you use routines in that way. 

On top of all of that, the developer asks that you create an account and hand over personal information BEFORE you can even test it! 

Those are all CONS. Usually in a review you’d also list PROS but any pros I can find are so trivial compared to all of the problems listed above that I don’t want to include them for fear of giving someone the wrong impression that the good counterbalances the bad.

Stay far away from this app in its current state. It will not help you.

author: ThisIsDill

title: It just works
body:
I’m at a loss for an explanation. I’ve been using these kinds of apps for years, I’ve probably tried a hundred but none of them came close to this one. I find myself using the Apple Watch & my iPhone to keep up on alerts.

My first impression wasn’t so great though. Why aren’t there streaks, graphs, badges, statistics, and other useless vanities? Because they’re distractions.

The simplicity of the app keeps you focused on getting the next task done and not sweating any of the unimportant details.

There’s no “delay this task for 10 minutes button” or any of that other garbage that helps you procrastinate — remember that this is for people who may have trouble with organization and procrastination.

There are definitely some things I would improve and some other things I would add but all in all it works.

title: Paywall doesn’t help people who need it
body:
I want to try your app without being preyed upon. Let me try it for 14 days without putting in payment info, you scammers. Your business model depends on people forgetting about their trials and you know it. You’re not trying to help people with autism or adhd at all, you’re trying to steal from them for trying to test your product. What BS. I’ll try again and I’ll edit my rating when the trial is actually free :)

Also, where is my option to make use of the option for an actually free account? You’re double-charging some users to allegedly help other users get access, so how do I, as a low income person, get the free version other people are paying for so you can offer it?

Or are you stealing their money and not offering any actual free accounts?

Response to the developer response: I know how app development works. Do in-app charges after a free trial but don’t make people put in payment information for free trials. That’s sleazy. Don’t prey upon people by expecting them to forget to cancel. We are talking about autistic folks with ADHD. Don’t gaslight me — you know exactly what you’re doing here.

title: So close! - updated.
body:
Update: After hearing from Signe I’m going up a star for getting a response and that the developers listen to feedback and implement features the users are asking for. I know that seems simple but it’s not common. I put a lot of thought into my review and came from a perspective of wanting to improve on the user’s experience so I enjoyed hearing back. Cheers, Tiimo! 

I had ADHD and I heard that Tiimo is a great app for your schedule so I downloaded it and it’s almost perfect, but there’s one feature that makes it frustrating for me to use. When I’m creating a routine or activity I want to be able to use the length of time an activity takes instead of a start and stop time. It might seem small, but I have time blindness so I time myself doing activities and record the amount of time they take to complete. Then I use that to schedule. Ideally I would place it on my schedule at the time I want to start and the end time would generate. With the start and stop time, whenever I want to place an item on my schedule at a different time it’s frustrating to first determine the amount of time the task takes, then reset the start and end time. Otherwise I really enjoy this app.

title: Updating my review
body:
I’m updating my review again from 3 stars to 4. The app has improved since I started using it, and some of the bugs have been worked out. One issue I reported was fixed within a couple of days. Also, one issue that I assumed was a bug went away when I upgraded to a newer iPad. I can see that the developers are really making an effort to make the app better. 

This is a very unique app, and I haven’t found another like it. I have ADHD and autism, and it works with the way my brain works. I have executive dysfunction, and I have a hard time getting started on tasks. Seeing the notification that a task is about to start kind of creates a sense of urgency to get started. And it keeps me on task. And because I’m a visual thinker, I like that you can customize the color and icons. Calendars have never worked for me, partly because you can never exactly guess how long a task will take and unexpected things come up. This app is flexible in that it lets you start and finish tasks early or late. So it’s pretty cool, and I think it helps me a lot.

author: marsyd75

title: Awesome potential, some bugs still need working out
body:
I love this concept. I think the format has great potential for helping anyone who needs a little extra structure in their life. Just gotta be patient while they work out the kinks.

Pretty quick after downloading I ran into a bug though. I was trying to change the icon for an activity to a custom icon. When the app requested permission for my photos, I changed my mind and wanted to go back to the built in icon options. So I tapped on the x for the request camera/gallery access window, but instead of collapsing the window it just regenerated the same window. So unless I allow access to the camera/gallery or restart the app I am stuck on that screen. Pretty minor bug.

Also, it’d be really cool to have overlapping events show a visual depiction of the time overlap instead of a warning (if that makes sense...?). For example, I put laundry as a 4 hour activity since it takes that long, but I can do other activities during that time as well, so I don’t need to be alerted of the overlap between those activities

I’m excited to keep trying this app!

title: Like this so far
body:

Time management and executive function are hard for me. I can set up my day the night before and then I’m free to just be myself knowing that I won’t forget to do something important at the right time. 

3 stars because I’m new and haven’t used it much yet. There is some functionality I’d like to see added. Namely an ability to do customized repetitions. Also setting times for activities is slightly glitchy. I’ve had to delete and recreate and activity already because the end time wouldn’t stay set to what I put it at after I hit save. It worked the second time though. 

All in all really interested to see how this works for me and how the app developers improve it over time.

title: Top notch privacy policy - please add audible reminders
body:
Tiimo Privacy policy is the best. Don’t let people steal & sell your kid’s information for a cheap app! 

Easy to use, add your repeating or single events, choose icon & colour. Determine if event can start or end early. It reminds with a banner and shows the amount of time remaining. Swipe to end early.

I decided not to keep this app because it doesn’t have audible alarms. This app is for someone who is willing to monitor their own device for reminders, not for the easily distracted or those that need constant reminders.

Please add audible alarms! Banners are not enough for distracted kids. Screaming monkeys, tiger roars or mom’s recorded (pleasant, not screaming) voice are all acceptable options. 

Please add secondary (optional) distraction alarm that can beep every n minutes for easily distracted kids. 

These 2 things are all this app needs to put parents out of the nagging business!
